FOMC Polymarket odds increasingly favor the Federal Reserve leaving interest rates unchanged at its October meeting, with the probability of another rate hike falling sharply despite persistent inflation concerns.
According to the latest Polymarket figures, the odds of the Fed holding rates steady stand at 87%, while the probability of a 25-basis-point increase has dropped to 14%. The market assigns less than a 1% chance to a rate cut or a larger increase.
The figures suggest traders expect Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to take a wait-and-see approach at their October 27–28 meeting. The contract has attracted tens of millions of dollars in trading volume, reflecting significant interest in the central bank’s next move.
However, expectations have shifted considerably in recent weeks. After hotter-than-expected inflation data, the probability of an October hike climbed toward 50% before retreating as investors reassessed the likelihood of consecutive hikes.
FOMC Polymarket Odds: Inflation Keeps Rate Hike Debate Alive
The latest US consumer price index (CPI) report showed annual inflation accelerating to 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August. Core inflation also increased, reinforcing concerns that price pressures could remain above the Fed’s 2% target.
Nevertheless, some policymakers have argued against rushing into another increase. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said on October 14 that further hikes could be necessary to control persistent inflation but stressed there was no urgency to act at the upcoming meeting.
That distinction appears central to current market pricing: traders are not ruling out additional tightening, but increasingly expect policymakers to wait for more evidence before moving again.

Social Media and Market Commentary Reflect Uncertainty
Discussion among prediction-market traders has highlighted the competing arguments. In a recent Reddit discussion in the r/Polymarket community, participants pointed to the September inflation figures and elevated energy costs as reasons a hike could remain possible, while also noting that earlier comments from Fed officials had reduced expectations of immediate action.
Warsh has added another layer of uncertainty by declining to signal the committee’s next move publicly. Speaking at an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok on October 16, he said he does not prejudge individual meetings.
The lack of explicit forward guidance leaves traders particularly sensitive to incoming economic data and any remaining policy signals.
What Comes Next for Fed Rate Expectations?
With the October meeting approaching, Polymarket’s current pricing makes a pause the clear favorite, though odds can shift quickly as new information emerges.
A fresh inflation surprise could revive bets on a hike, while softer economic data or further calls for patience from policymakers could reinforce expectations of unchanged rates.
For now, traders appear to favor caution over immediate tightening. The key question is whether the Fed sees inflation as sufficiently persistent to justify another hike, or whether policymakers will wait until December before deciding their next move.

articles.title: Gold and silver prices pressured by hot inflation, but gold ETF holdings buck trend to hit 2026 highs – Heraeus - Kitco
articles.summary: Gold and silver prices pressured by hot inflation, but gold ETF holdings buck trend to hit 2026 highs – Heraeus  KitcoGold Slides for Third Straight Session  TradingViewGold price prediction today: Will gold prices be range-bound? Check outlook for October 19, 2026 week  The Times of IndiaGold slips amid stronger dollar, bond sell-off, and a pullback in losses in oil  Investing.com IndiaGold, silver futures rise as global cues improve and Fed rate hike con...
articles.full_text:
(Kitco News) – Gold and silver both came under renewed pressure following last week’s elevated CPI and PPI prints. Still, gold ETF demand has bucked the earlier trend to rise to annual highs despite the oil and rate headwinds. At the same time, India’s evolving import tax rules continue to impact precious metals demand, according to precious metals analysts at Heraeus.
In their latest update, the analysts noted that gold prices held critical support levels last week amidst a challenging macro backdrop.
“Gold briefly wicked below $4,100/oz following the September US CPI release, as the initially hawkish market reaction pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher and increased expectations for another Fed hike,” they noted. “That reaction has since partly reversed, with the implied probability of a 25 bp increase at the 28 October meeting falling and gold recovering the support at $4,100/oz as yields and the dollar have eased.”
Gold ETF holdings have also climbed to their highest levels of the year to date despite the significant pressures on the gold price.
“Bloomberg-tracked holdings reached a year-to-date peak of 101.3 moz on 8 October, up 5.3% from the year-to-date low of 96.2 moz on 20 July and around 2% higher than at the start of the year,” the analysts noted. “Holdings have since remained just above 101 moz, even as gold has struggled at around $4,100-4,200/oz, well below its January peak.”
“For much of 2026, changes in ETF holdings have broadly tracked the gold price, falling during the correction from the January high before recovering as prices rebounded through August, but the two have since diverged,” they said. “ETF holdings often lag turning points in the price, as investors tend to hold positions, or add on dips, in anticipation of a renewed rally until it becomes clear that one is not imminent. Demand has also broadened geographically, with Asian-listed funds accounting for almost half of the increase in global holdings over the 12 months to September, compared with around 30% from US-listed funds and 20% from Europe.”
And after being among the largest sovereign buyers of 2026, the central bank of Kazakhstan is reducing its gold holdings.
“The National Bank of Kazakhstan plans to lower gold's share of its international reserves from around 78% to 75% by year-end, after holdings climbed to 386 tonnes,” the analysts said. “The bank was the world's fourth-largest reported central-bank buyer through August, adding around 36 tonnes during the first eight months of the year. The planned reduction will be split between options and sales of physical bullion, as elevated US Treasury yields increase the relative appeal of dollar assets and the central bank seeks to reduce concentration risk in its reserves.”
“At current reserve values, a 3-percentage-point reduction in gold's share would represent roughly 15 tonnes of gold exposure, although the amount of physical metal sold will depend on prices and the use of derivatives,” they noted. “The move is therefore primarily a portfolio rebalancing exercise rather than evidence of a broader reversal in central-bank gold demand.”
Spot gold continued to trade near session lows early in the early part of the North American session, and last traded at $4,151.80 per ounce for a loss of 0.33% on the daily chart.
Turning to silver, Heraeus analysts pointed out that the gray metal was also under pressure following last week’s hotter-than-expected inflation reports.
“The silver price fell through support around $60/oz and briefly approached the July lows around $55/oz, as the data strengthened expectations for another Fed rate hike and initially pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher,” they said. “That reaction has subsequently eased, with the implied probability of a 25 bp increase at the 28 October meeting falling to below 30%, while the 10-year Treasury yield and dollar have both moved lower, down from recent yearly highs. Silver consequently recovered above $57/oz, although the break below $60/oz leaves the technical picture weaker and highlights the metal’s sensitivity to changes in real yields and monetary-policy expectations.”
And India’s import tax regime for precious metals continues to evolve, impacting banks and wholesale demand.
“The Indian government has confirmed that silver, gold and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies are subject to 3% Integrated Goods and Services Tax,” the analysts wrote. “The government said on 8 October that the exemption for these channels had not been extended beyond 31 March, putting all import routes on an equal tax footing. Banks have, in practice, been paying the tax since April, after a month-long pause in imports while the rules were unclear. As the levy is recoverable as an input tax credit, its main effect is on working capital rather than final costs, and the confirmation removes uncertainty rather than adding a new obstacle to Indian silver imports. India imported 232 moz of silver in 2025, equivalent to around 20% of global demand.”
Silver prices were also giving back some of their early gains on Monday morning, but they remained in positive territory on the session.
Spot silver last traded at $57.318 per ounce for a gain of 0.61% on the daily chart.

articles.title: Dow Jones Futures Prediction: Index Closes at 52,002 After 0.3% Drop as Investors Weigh Inflation, Oil Prices & Fed Rate Risks; Check Monday Market Outlook, Key Things to Watch - The Sunday Guardian
articles.summary: Dow Jones Futures Prediction: Index Closes at 52,002 After 0.3% Drop as Investors Weigh Inflation, Oil Prices & Fed Rate Risks; Check Monday Market Outlook, Key Things to Watch  The Sunday Guardian
articles.full_text:
Dow Jones Futures Prediction: The Dow Jones futures prediction for Monday, October 19, 2026, will depend on investor sentiment following the latest Wall Street session, movements in crude oil prices and expectations surrounding US inflation and Federal Reserve policy. Investors will also monitor corporate earnings and developments in technology stocks for clues about the next trading session.
With US markets closed over the weekend, futures trading when markets reopen could provide an early indication of investor positioning. However, futures movements do not guarantee that the Dow Jones Industrial Average will open in the same direction or maintain that trend throughout Monday’s session.
Dow Jones Futures: How Wall Street Closed on Friday
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 175.28 points, or 0.34%, to close at 52,002.41 on Friday, October 16, according to the Associated Press. The S&P 500 declined 1.09% to 7,659.44, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.15% to 26,140.03. Technology and semiconductor shares led the broader sell-off.
The weekly performance was more mixed. The Dow gained approximately 0.7% for the week, while the S&P 500 fell 1.9% and the Nasdaq lost 4.5%. This divergence suggests that weakness in technology stocks weighed more heavily on the broader market than on the blue-chip Dow index.
Dow Jones Futures Prediction for Monday, October 19
The short-term outlook remains uncertain, with several factors likely to determine whether Dow futures recover or extend Friday’s losses.
- Bullish outlook: A recovery in blue-chip shares, easing oil prices and improved investor confidence could support a rebound.
- Bearish outlook: Persistent inflation, rising energy costs and further weakness in technology stocks could pressure US equity futures.
- Sideways outlook: Investors may remain cautious ahead of further economic data and corporate earnings, limiting major moves until a clearer market signal emerges.
These scenarios are conditional. The actual direction will depend on futures prices and new developments when trading resumes.
Dow Jones Futures Outlook: Inflation Remains a Major Concern
US inflation is one of the biggest economic factors for Wall Street this week. The Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% year over year in September, up from 3.4% in August. Monthly inflation increased 0.6%, while core CPI, which excludes food and energy, climbed 2.6% year over year.
Persistent inflation could make it more difficult for the Federal Reserve to ease monetary policy. Investors will watch economic releases and comments from policymakers for indications of whether interest rates could remain elevated or rise further.
The Federal Open Market Committee is scheduled to meet on October 27–28, making the upcoming policy decision another potential source of volatility for US stocks.
Crude Oil Prices: Another Key Driver for Dow Futures
Oil prices surged on Friday, adding to concerns about inflation and corporate costs. West Texas Intermediate crude settled at $101.41 a barrel, while Brent crude rose to $109.86, according to Dow Jones Newswires reporting carried by The Wall Street Journal. Supply concerns linked to geopolitical tensions contributed to the gains.
Higher energy prices can affect the Dow in different ways. Energy producers may benefit from stronger crude prices, while industrial, transportation and consumer companies could face increased expenses. A further rise in oil could also complicate the inflation outlook.
Technology Stocks and AI Investment Concerns
Technology and semiconductor shares remain important factors for the wider US stock market. On Friday, Micron Technology fell 5.6% and Intel declined 5.8%, reflecting continued pressure on chipmakers. The Nasdaq’s 4.5% weekly decline was substantially steeper than the Dow’s weekly performance.
Investors are reassessing whether the expected returns from substantial artificial intelligence infrastructure spending will justify the costs. Further weakness in chipmakers and AI-related companies could weigh on market sentiment, although the Dow’s performance will also depend on its industrial, financial, healthcare and consumer-facing constituents.
Dow Jones Futures Prediction: Key Things to Watch on Monday
Investors tracking Dow Jones futures on October 19 should focus on the following factors:
- Overnight futures movement: Check whether Dow futures rise or fall before the opening bell.
- Crude oil prices: Watch whether Brent and WTI remain near elevated levels or retreat.
- Federal Reserve expectations: Monitor changes in rate expectations ahead of the October 27–28 meeting.
- Technology and semiconductor stocks: Further losses could weigh on the broader market.
- Corporate earnings: Company results and forward guidance may influence individual Dow constituents.
- Treasury yields: Changes in bond yields can affect equity valuations and investor appetite for risk.
These indicators can help investors assess the opening outlook, but none independently determines the direction of the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Dow Jones Futures Prediction: Will the Index Rise or Fall on Monday?
The outlook for Monday remains uncertain, with risks on both sides. The Dow’s weekly gain offers some evidence of relative resilience, but Friday’s decline, elevated oil prices and persistent inflation concerns could limit the potential for a sustained recovery.
A rebound could develop if investors return to blue-chip shares and energy prices stabilise. However, further selling in technology stocks or renewed concerns about interest rates could put pressure on futures.
The closing level of 52,002.41 is a reference point for the previous cash-market session, not a forecast for Monday’s futures price. The actual outlook should be reassessed using live futures quotations when trading resumes.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
What is the Dow Jones futures prediction for Monday, October 19, 2026?
The near-term outlook is cautious and volatile. Inflation, oil prices, Federal Reserve expectations and technology-stock performance will be among the main factors influencing market direction.
Where did the Dow Jones close on Friday?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 52,002.41 on October 16, 2026, down 175.28 points, or approximately 0.34%.
Why are Dow Jones futures important?
Dow futures provide an indication of how investors are positioning ahead of the regular US stock market session. They can move in response to economic data, corporate announcements and global developments, but they do not guarantee the cash market’s opening direction.
How could inflation affect the Dow Jones?
Higher inflation can increase expectations of tighter monetary policy, potentially putting pressure on share valuations. It can also raise operating costs for businesses and reduce consumers’ purchasing power.
What is the next major Federal Reserve event?
The next scheduled Federal Open Market Committee meeting is October 27–28, 2026. Investors will monitor the decision and accompanying communications for clues about the future interest-rate path.

articles.title: Prediction Markets Raise Odds of No Fed Rate Hike in October - KuCoin
articles.summary: Prediction Markets Raise Odds of No Fed Rate Hike in October  KuCoin
articles.full_text:
As Fed Chair Kevin Warsh refused to preview the October 28 rate decision on October 16, 2026, during an IMF (International Monetary Fund) fireside chat in Bangkok, saying he does not prejudge meetings, prediction markets sharply raised their odds of no change.
On Friday, at the time of reporting, the probability of a no rate change in the Fed’s October decision surged to an all-time high (ATH) of 87%, according to data Finbold analyzed from Polymarket, a top-tier decentralized prediction market platform.
The odds of a 25 basis points (bps) rate hike in October were at 14%. The Federal Reserve raised its interest rates by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4.00%, during its September 16 policy decision.
At press time, the no-change outcome had a reported volume of $13.15 million compared to $9.97 million for the 25bps increase.
Warsh was asked about the direction of U.S. monetary policy and the prospects for another interest-rate increase at the Federal Reserve’s upcoming October 28 meeting.
Warsh responded with a non-committal stance, which markets interpreted as leaving the door open to a pause, thereby prompting a sharp rise in the probability of no rate hike in October.
What’s next for Fed’s rate decision in 2026
At the time of writing, the odds of zero Fed rate cuts by the end of 2026 had climbed to 96.8%, signaling high conviction largely due to the recent sticky inflation.
What’s in it for cryptocurrencies?
Most of the cryptocurrencies remained trapped in a correction phase over the past seven days through October 16, driven by hotter-than-expected inflation data from the United States.
As a result, a possible no-rate change in the upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, could rejuvenate bullish sentiment.

Gold rises ₹461 to ₹1,48,379 per 10 grams, while silver gains ₹826 to ₹2,12,013 per kg on MCX as easing US Fed rate hike fears support precious metals.
New Delhi: Gold and silver prices moved higher in early trading on Monday, October 19, supported by positive global market trends and easing concerns over another interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve.
Both precious metals recorded gains on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), with investors closely watching US inflation data and upcoming Federal Reserve policy decisions.
Gold Price Today: MCX Gold Rises ₹461
On the MCX, December gold futures climbed ₹461, or 0.31 per cent, to ₹1,48,379 per 10 grams, compared with the previous closing price of ₹1,47,918.
Gold touched an intraday high of ₹1,48,499, gaining ₹581, while its lowest level during early trading stood at ₹1,48,120.
Silver Price Today: MCX Silver Crosses ₹2.12 Lakh
Silver futures for December delivery increased ₹826, or 0.39 per cent, to ₹2,12,013 per kilogram from the previous close of ₹2,11,187.
The white metal reached an intraday high of ₹2,12,750, while its session low stood at ₹2,11,634.
US Federal Reserve Decision In Focus
Commodity experts said comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reduced expectations of an October interest rate increase to below 20 per cent.
However, stronger US inflation figures continue to create uncertainty over a possible December rate hike.
Investors will closely monitor the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for October 27–28.
International Gold And Silver Prices Rise
In international markets, COMEX gold advanced towards $4,200 per ounce, gaining around 0.50 per cent.
COMEX silver also strengthened, moving towards $57.80 per ounce, up approximately 0.89 per cent.
A stronger Indian rupee, however, limited some domestic price gains.
Gold And Silver Price Outlook
Market analysts identified immediate resistance for MCX gold at ₹1,48,600, followed by ₹1,50,000–₹1,50,700. Support is expected near ₹1,48,000.
For silver, resistance lies between ₹2,14,000 and ₹2,15,000, while immediate support is placed around ₹2,07,000–₹2,08,000.
The upcoming US Fed decision and inflation trends are expected to influence precious metal prices.

articles.title: Fed Rate Hike Fears: SoftBank’s $164B Debt Could Rattle Crypto Markets - Coin Gabbar
articles.summary: Fed Rate Hike Fears: SoftBank’s $164B Debt Could Rattle Crypto Markets  Coin Gabbar
articles.full_text:
A viral post says SoftBank's debt is growing fast just as Fed rate hike worries are rising, and traders are asking whether the stress could reach crypto.
We checked each claim against the company's own filings and the Federal Reserve's official pages.
Some numbers hold up well. Others are market prices that no official source can confirm, and we mark them clearly. The original post is linked for reference.
SoftBank's Q1 financial report lists total borrowings of about ¥26.6 trillion at June 30, 2026. That is roughly $164 billion at the quarter-end exchange rate (our conversion), so the headline figure is right.
One detail matters: this covers the whole group, including units like SoftBank Corp. The parent company's own debt is ¥12.2 trillion, or about $75B.
The report links the jump in interest costs to an $11.5B loan backed by Arm shares from December 2025 and $20B drawn from bridge loans in April 2026.
Some loans are also "non-recourse," meaning lenders can claim only the pledged shares, not the parent's other assets.
The report puts roughly ¥5.4 trillion in that group, backed by Arm shares, SoftBank Corp. shares and other holdings.
| Claim in the post | What official sources show | 
| Debt of $164B at June 2026 | Confirmed (group total, our conversion) | 
| Interest cost about $2B, up 95% | Finance cost ¥328.7B (about $2.0B), up 98.9% on last year | 
| New $11B raised at up to 9.75% | Confirmed: about $11.1B, highest 9.75% | 
| Extra $1B interest each year | Our math: about $1.03B a year | 
| Stock down 25%; default cover at 424 bps | Market data, not in filings, unverified | 
On September 24, SoftBank announced dollar and euro notes worth about $11.1 billion, with issue expected on September 29.
Both S&P and Fitch rate them BB+, one notch below investment grade. They carry no collateral and no guarantee.
| Notes | Size | Interest | Matures | 
| USD 2030 | $1.0B | 8.625% | Apr 2030 | 
| USD 2032 | $4.5B | 9.25% | Apr 2032 | 
| USD 2034 | $4.5B | 9.75% | Apr 2034 | 
| EUR 2030 | €0.5B | 7.125% | Oct 2030 | 
| EUR 2032 | €0.5B | 8.0% | Oct 2032 | 
Adding the yearly coupons gives about $1.03 billion, which matches the post's figure.
On October 1, SoftBank confirmed it paid the third and final $10 billion installment of a $30 billion follow-on investment in OpenAI.
The first two installments were paid on April 1 and July 1, at a pre-money valuation of $730B, per the Q1 report.
Total invested is now $64.6 billion, for a stake of about 13%. The bond sale paid for this last installment.
The bond sale also closed out a temporary loan. The company's $40 billion bridge loan, signed in March with five banks, was due on March 25, 2027.
Per the October 1 release, all borrowings under it are repaid and the unused $10 billion was cancelled.
Investors mainly worry about profit, and the first-quarter results are mixed:
Net income was ¥347.3B, down 17.7% on last year.
Most investment gains came from Intel shares (¥1,332.9B), while no gain was booked on OpenAI.
Cash fell to ¥3.93 trillion from ¥5.36 trillion.
The report states there is no doubt about the company continuing as a going concern.
The Federal Reserve raised rates by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.00% on September 16, in a unanimous vote, and called inflation still elevated.
Its projections put the middle forecast for the end of 2026 at 4.1%, which points to one more quarter-point rise. Officials also expect PCE inflation of 3.7% this year.
The BLS reported September consumer prices up 3.7% over the year. Higher rates make new borrowing pricier, and SoftBank's new bonds already pay between 7.1% and 9.75%.
The next policy meeting is on October 27–28, according to the Fed's calendar. Markets will be watching whether another Fed rate hike lands in October or December.
No official source ties SoftBank's debt to coin prices. The link is mostly mood. Many traders treat crypto as a risk asset, so shaky AI-related stocks or rising rate fears can weigh on sentiment.
That is a common pattern, not a promise.
If you follow a Fed rate hike and its effect on coins, these are the signals to watch:
The October 27–28 decision and the wording of its statement
The next US inflation report
New filings on SoftBank's press release page
Pressure from the Fed is real, and SoftBank's numbers are huge. Yet the official papers show a company that repaid its short-term loan, sold bonds rated BB+ and reported no going-concern doubt.
The post's debt figures mostly check out, while its market-price claims remain unverified. Treat this as a risk to watch, not a verdict. This is information, not financial advice.

articles.summary: Nasdaq Future Prediction Tomorrow: Will Nasdaq Futures Open Higher or Lower on Monday? Check US Stock Market Outlook, Oil Prices, Bank Earnings Ahead of September CPI — What Investors Should Know  The Sunday Guardian
articles.full_text:
Nasdaq Futures Prediction LIVE: The Wall Street kicks off its trading session on Monday, October 19, amid inflation, interest rate policy by the US central bank, higher oil costs and apprehension over investments in artificial intelligence technology.
The Nasdaq Composite ended Friday, October 16, at 26,140.03, having dipped by about 2.15% and the S&P 500 dropped by 1.09% to 7,659.44, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average decreased by 0.34% to 52,002.41.
US Stock Market Prediction for Monday
The outlook of the US stock market is still one of caution while the investors will be looking out for any signs of stability following the fall in the Nasdaq by about 4.5 percent for the week. On its part, the Dow rose by about 0.7 percent and this shows that the market is tilting towards defensive shares.
Nasdaq Futures Tomorrow, October 19
The Nasdaq futures may still be volatile after the session is resumed since the initial move will depend on how the semiconductors perform, as well as the yield of Treasuries and the appetite of the investors in AI-related stocks. The trader needs to differentiate between the Nasdaq-100 futures and Nasdaq Composite since their price levels differ.
Nasdaq Futures Prediction: Why Monday Could Be Important
Monday’s trading may determine whether Friday’s selloff is just a correction or the start of something more substantial. The market will determine whether investors get back into tech stocks or keep selling expensive growth shares. Any buying across the board would be good for the recovery prospects, but a further decline in semiconductors may hurt the broader market.
Nasdaq Futures Prediction: Nvidia Earnings in Focus
Nvidia is still an important company to watch since its demand for AI chips has contributed to valuations of technology companies. The main issues to look out for will be revenue growth, data center demand, margin performance and management commentary. Positive performance can help bolster the semiconductor sector but even good results won’t move the stock market if there is too much investment into AI infrastructure.
Nasdaq Futures Prediction: Why CPI Matters for Stocks

articles.title: Why the Bond Market Is Defying the Fed's Hawkish Inflation Stance - InteractiveCrypto
articles.summary: Why the Bond Market Is Defying the Fed's Hawkish Inflation Stance  InteractiveCrypto
articles.full_text:
The financial markets are caught in an escalating tension between a Federal Reserve determined to tame persistent inflation and a bond market signaling deeper caution about future economic vitality. Recent data and official commentary highlight a widening divergence between short-term monetary resolve and long-term economic confidence.
On September 16, 2026, the Federal Reserve lifted its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%, lifting the effective federal funds rate to 3.75%. While the central bank intended to signal an unyielding stance against lingering price pressures, the bond market's reaction has complicated the picture, with long-term yields tumbling faster than short-term paper.
Inflation Pressures Persist Against Fed Resolve
The Fed's hawkish posture remains rooted in stubbornly resilient price data. The September 2026 Consumer Price Index demonstrated continued momentum, rising 0.65% month-over-month to reach an index level of 336.298. Headline CPI stood at 3.7% year-on-year, while core gauges remained well above the central bank's target. Producer prices further illustrated the challenge, surging 1.3% month-over-month in September to drive the annual wholesale rate to 6.3%. Together, the figures reinforce why central bankers hesitate to declare victory over inflation.
The Yield Curve Reprices Long-Run Growth
Despite the inflation backdrop, Treasury trading has delivered a starkly counter-intuitive message. On October 15, 2026, the 10-year Treasury yield slid 9.0 basis points to finish at 5.10%, while the 2-year yield slipped 5.0 basis points to close at 4.77%.
This 4.0-basis-point gap in yield movements is critical. The 2-year yield closely reflects near-term policy expectations, while the 10-year yield mirrors long-term growth and structural economic expectations. When the 10-year yield drops considerably faster than the 2-year, it demonstrates that markets are more worried about impending economic deceleration than persistent Fed tightening. The 10-year minus 2-year Treasury yield spread, which stood at 37 basis points on October 14, compressed to 33 basis points on October 15 before adjusting to 35 basis points on October 16, keeping traders alert to fresh inversion risks.
Fed Communication Prompts Traders to Bet on an October Pause
Official communications have amplified market uncertainty. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking on October 16, 2026, acknowledged the recent hike and elevated inflation but deliberately declined to telegraph policy decisions, remarking that he does not prejudge meetings and that upcoming gatherings represent crystallising moments.
Traders interpreted the measured tone as tacit support for a policy pause in October. Interest-rate futures have adjusted to price only around a 30% probability of an immediate hike in late October, with consensus expecting the central bank to hold before potentially delivering a final quarter-point adjustment in December.
Debt Strains and Cross-Asset Repercussions
The macroeconomic landscape faces additional strain from the expanding federal balance sheet, with national debt surpassing $40 trillion. On October 14, 2026, the International Monetary Fund cautioned that the United States cannot simply rely on baseline growth to outpace its debt obligations, urging prompt fiscal consolidation. The U.S. Treasury countered on October 15, rejecting the warning and questioning the IMF's historical forecasting record.
Cross-asset markets reflect these intersecting anxieties. Major equity indices faced downward pressure in mid-October before finding support following Warsh's commentary. Gold advanced on October 15 as bond yields retreated, while the U.S. dollar eased. Concurrently, digital assets like Bitcoin experienced risk-off selling, with correlation to 10-year real yields hitting notable highs as fiscal sustainability entered investor focus. Investors evaluating multi-asset portfolios amid these macro shifts often use platforms like eToro to monitor cross-asset positioning.
Key Catalysts Ahead
Upcoming economic reports will test whether the bond market's growth concerns or the Fed's inflation fears prove accurate. The calendar features the September Housing Starts report on October 20 alongside building permits, followed by weekly jobless claims on October 22. These releases will provide fresh insight into consumer resilience and labor conditions ahead of the Fed's late-October policy decision.

articles.title: Is this the beginning of the AI bubble burst, or just a healthy correction? Japanese stocks shaken by the CoreWeave shock and higher-than-expected US CPI: What individual investors should check this week｜日本個別株デューデリジェンスセンター - note
articles.summary: Is this the beginning of the AI bubble burst, or just a healthy correction? Japanese stocks shaken by the CoreWeave shock and higher-than-expected US CPI: What individual investors should check this week｜日本個別株デューデリジェンスセンター  note
articles.full_text:
On October 6, when the Nikkei Stock Average hit 70,683 yen, recovering to the 70,000-yen level for the first time in three months, a bright mood spread across the market. However, in less than 10 days since then, the atmosphere has changed completely. In the Tokyo market on October 15, the Nikkei fell by 3,318 yen in a single day, closing at 64,426 yen. This was a record-breaking plunge, marking the third-largest decline in history.
The triggers were the sharp drop in corporate bonds of the US AI cloud company CoreWeave and the higher-than-expected US Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September, which was announced on the same day. The term "CoreWeave shock" is already becoming established in the market.
The Tokyo market rebounded on the weekend of the 16th, rising 898 yen. However, in the US market that night, CoreWeave shares were sold off again, and the Nasdaq Composite Index fell 572 points. Nikkei 225 futures in overnight trading ended at 63,630 yen, down 1,890 yen from the daytime closing price. The Tokyo market at the start of the week could face another difficult beginning.
"Is this the beginning of the AI bubble burst?" or "Is it just a healthy correction for a market that has risen too much?" Many individual investors are likely grappling with this question right now.
In this article, we will first organize what happened last week in chronological order, and confirm what is being viewed as problematic about the company CoreWeave and what the contents of the US CPI were. Then, we will carefully compare the arguments of both the bubble-burst camp and the healthy-correction camp. In the second half, we will summarize the events and indicators to check this week (October 19–23) in a checklist format, and finally, we will introduce five lesser-known stocks to watch that we want to unearth precisely because of this adjustment phase.
It will be a long article, but when the market is volatile, understanding the content rather than just the news headlines leads to calm judgment. Please stay with us until the end.
What happened last week: A timeline of the CoreWeave shock
October 13, night: Social media posts spark the fire
The origin of the CoreWeave shock was, unexpectedly, social media. On the night of October 13, US time, prominent venture investor Chamath Palihapitiya raised the issue on X (formerly Twitter), along with a screen showing that CoreWeave's corporate bond yields had reached 15%, questioning whether private credit (a loan market by lenders other than banks) might be in a bubble.
Furthermore, reports from the Financial Times that CoreWeave was seeking additional borrowing from insurance companies and others added to the pressure. The anxiety that had been simmering for some time—"Can AI infrastructure investment really continue to be fueled by debt?"—surfaced all at once.
According to the CNBC article mentioned above, the option trading volume for CoreWeave shares on the 14th exceeded seven times the 30-day average, and purchases of put options to prepare for a price decline reached nearly 200,000 contracts. This is almost double the number of call options (about 106,000 contracts) betting on a price increase. It shows that investors rushed to buy "insurance" in preparation for further declines. The stock prices of companies like Nebius Group and IREN, which also rent out GPUs for AI, also fell by up to 10%.
October 14: US CPI upside surprise and CoreWeave sharp drop coincide on the same day
The 14th was also the day the September CPI was announced in the US. The headline index rose 3.7% year-on-year, exceeding the market forecast of 3.6% and accelerating from 3.4% in August. The core index, excluding food and energy, also rose 2.6% year-on-year, exceeding the forecast of 2.5%.
Following the re-acceleration of inflation, the US 10-year Treasury yield briefly exceeded 5.3%, and two concerns—"rising interest rates" and "anxiety over AI companies' funding"—erupted simultaneously. CoreWeave shares fell 15.5% that day to close at $65.78, the S&P 500 fell 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite Index fell about 1.9%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) saw a significant drop of about 4%.
On the same day, the 14th, Chinese semiconductor manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) indicated its policy to introduce new server memory products with higher storage density within the year. With increased competition from Chinese firms in mind, the sell-off spread to semiconductor stocks in Asia, starting with major South Korean semiconductor companies. Some in the market have called this the "CXMT shock."
October 15: Nikkei average down 3,318 yen, the third-largest drop in history
The turmoil in the US market hit the Tokyo market the following day, the 15th. Selling concentrated on major semiconductor and AI-related stocks such as Advantest, Tokyo Electron, and SoftBank Group, and the Nikkei average fell 3,255 yen in the morning session alone. The closing price was 64,426 yen, down 3,318 yen (4.90%) from the previous day, sinking to its lowest level in about a month since September 17.
According to the views of market participants published in Rakuten Securities' investment information media "Toshiru," there was an eerie feeling in the fact that the stock market was trying to recover even though US long-term interest rates had risen to the 5% range, and the sharp drop in CoreWeave's corporate bonds pulled the trigger. It has also been pointed out that Kioxia Holdings, which had gained popularity among individual investors in the first half of 2026, also saw its price drop significantly, and that the stop-loss selling of stocks bought on margin may have accelerated the decline.
October 16: Rebound on CEO's remarks, but sold off again on Friday night
The tide turned once on the 15th in the US market. Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, which is also a major shareholder in CoreWeave, responded to an interview with Bloomberg at an event in Stockholm, expressing his view that CoreWeave's financial situation is stable and improving daily. Following this, CoreWeave shares rebounded by 5.94% to $69.69, and buying also returned to the Tokyo market on the 16th, centered on AI and semiconductor-related stocks. The Nikkei Stock Average ended the day up 898 yen at 65,324 yen, marking its first rebound in seven trading days.
However, in the US market on the 16th, CoreWeave shares plunged again by about 12%. Counting from the end of the previous week, it has lost about a quarter of its market capitalization in just one week.
What the CNBC article mentioned above emphasizes is that, more than the stock price decline, the sharp rise in corporate bond yields and the surge in credit default swaps (CDS) are serious. Even if the stock price falls, the company will not go bankrupt immediately, but it is a different story if it becomes unable to refinance its debt. That is exactly what the market is afraid of.
In the US market on Friday, selling also spread to large-cap tech stocks, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average ending down $175 at $52,002 and the Nasdaq Composite Index down 572 points at 26,140. The rise in crude oil prices against the backdrop of tensions in the Middle East is also acting as a headwind.
The Japanese edition of Newsweek explains that while the constituents of the SOX index lost more than $1 trillion in market capitalization in just six trading days, funds fled to defensive stocks such as healthcare and consumer-related sectors, causing the index to split in two. The S&P 500 rose to the 7,818-point level on October 6 before falling to the 7,600-point level, but it has barely managed to stay in positive territory for the month, making it difficult to see the severity of the decline by looking at the index alone.
Who is CoreWeave: Why is it called the 'canary in the coal mine'?
The Neo-Cloud business model
CoreWeave is a US company founded in 2017 that listed on the US Nasdaq market in March 2025. It builds data centers equipped with large numbers of Nvidia AI semiconductors (GPUs) and develops a business of lending that computing power to AI development companies and major cloud companies. Such 'cloud operators specializing in AI computing' are called Neo-Cloud.
Huge cloud operators like Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), and Amazon are called hyperscalers. They have huge earners outside of data centers, such as advertising, software, and online retail. Even if the recovery of AI investment is delayed, they can support it with cash earned from their core businesses.
On the other hand, Neo-Cloud is almost exclusively focused on AI. Because its revenue sources are limited, its creditworthiness is relatively low, and it must pay higher interest rates when borrowing money. The corporate bond rating for CoreWeave by the US rating agency S&P Global Ratings is 'B', which is five notches below the investment-grade floor of BBB minus, making it so-called junk grade.
In addition, Nvidia is both a major shareholder in CoreWeave and its GPU supplier. There have long been suggestions that funds and goods might be circulating among the same group of companies, and that AI demand might look larger than it actually is. This sharp drop is partly an eruption of doubts about that structure.
Sales have doubled, but debt has increased even more
To be clear, CoreWeave's business itself is growing rapidly. According to reports, management emphasized in an internal memo that the order backlog (the amount already contracted that will become revenue in the future) is large enough to cover debt repayment obligations, and told employees that the market sometimes moves irrationally.
However, according to an analysis by the US research firm Trefis, while sales more than doubled, up 115.3% in the year to June 2026, debt, which was $14.6 billion a year ago, has more than tripled. Operating cash flow also increased significantly from $638 million a year ago to $6.91 billion, but it is still not enough to cover the money going into capital investment

articles.title: Evercore flags key levels that could turn AI bull market into correction - Yahoo Finance Australia
articles.summary: Evercore flags key levels that could turn AI bull market into correction  Yahoo Finance Australia
articles.full_text:
Investing.com -- Last week's selloff in tech stocks marked the start of a "price discovery" process for the AI trade, Evercore strategists said, who identified specific market levels that, if breached, could turn the bull market into a correction or, in a recession scenario, a bear market.
"Last week reaffirms the notion "It Isn't Different This Time" amidst a perfect storm for the AI Bull highlighting lines in the sand that if crossed could morph the bull to correction, or bear," the team led by Julian Emanuel said in a note published Sunday.
The strategists flagged four stress points: investment-grade credit default swaps rising above their March peak of 68.33, high-yield credit default swaps breaking above their 411.04 peak, a reversal in the trend of upward earnings-per-share revisions, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbing above 5.62%.
Evercore's Washington policy team said that yield level could trigger a "fiscal wake up call," noting the recent peak of 5.36% makes 5.62% "a reasonable level to expect 'alarm bells' to sound."
Evercore pushed back on the idea that hyperscalers can issue debt without regard to market conditions to fund an estimated $1.3 trillion in AI capital spending for 2027, even as their free cash flow has turned negative. The strategists called that assumption "the stuff of fantasy," comparing it to the thinking that preceded the 2000 dot-com bust, the 2018 selloff tied to trade wars and Fed hikes, and Japan's 1989 bubble collapse, which was followed by 25 years of economic stagnation.
Until the flagged stress points are breached, Evercore said investors should "remain long AI" through what it calls the "AI class of 2026" stocks, while retaining hedges against volatility tied to the November 3 midterm elections through negative-beta stocks, S&P 500 straddles and Nasdaq-100 December put spread collars.
Investors should add to long positions and remove hedges if the Nasdaq-100 tests its 200-day moving average near 674, or if the S&P 500 tests 725, the strategists added.
Evercore reiterated its year-end 2026 S&P 500 price target of 7,750.

articles.title: Bond yields at 8 pc offer sweet spot for debt investors: Abhishek Bisen - The Federal
articles.summary: Bond yields at 8 pc offer sweet spot for debt investors: Abhishek Bisen  The Federal
articles.full_text:
Abhishek Bisen, Head of Fixed Income at Kotak Mahindra AMC, analyses rising G-sec yields, rate cycle timing, dynamic debt funds, and fixed-income risks.
Yields touching 8 per cent on longer-dated government and quasi-government bonds represent a historical "sweet spot" where risk-reward metrics become highly compelling for long-term investors. As central bank rate hikes, geopolitical conflict in West Asia, and rising US Treasury yields push domestic bond yields to multi-year highs, retail investors face crucial choices regarding asset allocation.
The Federal spoke to Abhishek Bisen, Head of Fixed Income and Fund Manager at Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company, to unpack the drivers behind surging yields, potential risks, and strategies for debt fund investors.
What factors are driving the recent surge in bond yields?
We can divide the drivers into internal issues and external issues, such as interest rates in developed economies and geopolitical risks.
Geopolitical conflicts in West Asia are keeping energy prices fairly high, injecting an element of uncertainty that remains at significantly elevated levels. In such scenarios, risk markets experience anxiety because it is difficult to fathom what is likely to happen. When risk-off sentiment takes hold, investors price off risk, and eventually all asset classes face pressure.
On the other hand, central banks across the developed world are raising interest rates and tightening monetary policy to contain inflationary pressures, which gets reflected in our economy as well.
Domestically, factors remain fairly under control. While inflation is rising and expected to rise further due to factors like monsoon conditions, current market pricing is discounting a fair amount of rate hikes by the central bank. Despite this, the bond market remains under pressure primarily due to global factors driving interest rates higher across our economy.
Should retail investors pause their equity Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) and shift money into debt funds?
That is a tricky question because it depends entirely on an investor's objective and risk appetite. All markets have experienced significant corrections. Equities, after correcting, offer long-term value. At the same time, fixed income investments have corrected significantly, driving yields to elevated levels.
It would be difficult to advise stopping equity SIPs to move entirely into fixed income. However, equity returns over the last couple of years have been somewhat muted, neutral, or negative in certain segments. Debt has performed relatively better over the last year or two compared to equities and commodities, depending on the time frame analyzed.
From an asset allocation perspective based on overall risk profiles, debt should be a prominent component today. The yield levels we have reached offer attractive value for long-term returns, offering assured-style returns if you remain in safer instruments like government bonds or AAA-rated corporate papers.
Longer-dated bond yields have touched almost 8 per cent or higher, which is a historical sweet spot. Whenever yields have crossed 8 per cent on the longer end of the curve, fixed income returns one or two years down the line have proven very attractive from a risk-reward perspective.
Investors should allocate to fixed income rather than staying overly conservative in overnight, savings account, or liquid options. You can incrementally increase risk within fixed income portfolios. While specific allocation depends on individual risk appetite, given current uncertainty, maintaining a slightly larger debt allocation of around 20 to 30 per cent makes sense from an overall risk perspective while keeping powder dry for potential future equity corrections.
Should investors lock in higher yields immediately or wait for interest rates to peak?
There is a quotation in our conference room: timing any market perfectly is accomplished either by liars or by people who get extremely lucky.
Because of this, we always recommend investors utilize SIPs or staggered allocations in fixed income at every level. Yield levels are currently attractive, and investors can keep accumulating over time.
A runaway move in interest rates is difficult to foresee. Furthermore, duration assets create significant volatility, which we have seen on a scale not witnessed in decades in the developed world. For instance, Japanese bond yields moved from below 1 per cent to around 3 per cent, while US bond yields climbed from around 1 per cent to above 5 per cent.
In India, an 8 per cent yield level represents a fairly decent number to accumulate long-term yields. While yields could move up slightly from current levels due to volatility, Government of India 30-year paper trades near 7.80 per cent, while State Development Loans (SDLs)—which are quasi-government instruments—already offer yields around 8.25 per cent. We have reached attractive numbers to begin allocating across these segments.
Which debt fund categories make the most sense in the current environment, and how do dynamic debt funds operate?
Fund managers continuously adjust duration based on forward-looking expectations and risk-reward dynamics. Dynamic duration funds offer the best solution for investors who are unsure where interest rates are heading.
At this point, funds remain somewhat conservative, but we are looking for opportunities to deploy cash and extend duration toward the higher end as clearer market signals emerge. Because investors dislike fixed income volatility, fund managers stay conservative during periods of extreme market movement.
Allocations toward the longer end look attractive, especially with State Development Loan yields touching 8.25 per cent and 30-year Government Securities trading around 7.80 per cent.
Regarding how dynamic debt funds work, fund managers exercise significant flexibility over duration. During favorable cycles, dynamic bond fund duration can extend to 9 or 10 years, or even higher—for example, gilt fund durations reached 11 to 12 years in past cycles. Currently, dynamic gilt durations sit around 4 to 5 years.
When yield curves flatten, we often employ a barbell strategy—allocating to both the short and long ends of the curve—which performs better than focusing purely on the short end. While shorter-duration funds provide psychological comfort, shorter-end yields can hurt the most when interest rates move up rapidly.
What primary risks should investors evaluate before investing in debt funds?
Duration risk is the primary factor investors must understand. However, duration risk gets mitigated if you remain invested for two, three, four, or five years—similar to how investors approach equity horizons.
Liquidity risk also gets mitigated over a long investment horizon. If volatility arises due to liquidity conditions, investors should remain invested rather than panic.
Credit risk requires extreme caution as we enter an era where credit quality becomes significantly important. Credit risk is often highest when market conditions appear deceptively calm, because the worst investment mistakes occur during good times.
Can investors lose money in debt funds even when bond yields are high?
Theoretically, when interest rates rise, bond prices fall, which can temporarily impact returns. However, over time, the accrual effect comes into play, helping offset initial price declines.
In extreme global scenarios—such as Japan or the US where 10-year yields surged from 1 per cent to 5 per cent, eroding up to 30 per cent of capital value—accrual income cannot easily cover the capital loss. But such extreme structural shifts rarely occur in India.
In India, if you invest in AAA-rated corporate bonds or high-quality sovereign paper with an investment horizon of 18 months or more, capital loss is exceptionally rare. You might experience periods where returns temporarily fall below bank fixed deposit rates, but future returns improve as the interest rate cycle turns over a two-to-three-year period.
What is the right strategy for both existing and first-time debt fund investors?
Because the entire yield curve is high, even investing in short-term debt funds is not a bad starting point for beginners. It helps first-time investors understand interest rate sensitivity, volatility, and how long it takes for accrual income to recover short-term mark-to-market fluctuations.
Investors should gradually progress from liquid and short-term funds toward longer-duration options. Retirement capital or long-term savings that will not be needed for years should be placed in long-term debt buckets. At current valuation levels, accrual income and eventual capital appreciation will cover portfolios over time, making long-term capital loss highly unlikely.
What is your outlook for bond yields and debt funds over the next few months?
The 10-year government bond yield reaching 7.40 per cent represents a key technical and psychological level. If technically breached, yields could head toward 7.60 per cent, though current levels already price in a significant amount of negative news. While yields might temporarily spike toward 8 per cent during periods of extreme global uncertainty, the odds of sustained higher spikes remain low. The broader yield trajectory is likely to move sideways or lower as clarity emerges.
For retail investors, tax changes have made direct inflows into pure debt funds more challenging. However, investors can access debt returns efficiently through hybrid categories, fund-of-funds, income-plus-opportunity schemes, arbitrage funds, or tax-efficient hybrid options like Solution-Oriented or Systematic Allocation funds. These categories combine debt stability with tax efficiency and potential equity upside, yielding better blended returns over a one-to-three-year horizon.

articles.title: Iran War Triggers Inflation, Central Bank Raises Interest Rates - VOI.ID
articles.summary: Iran War Triggers Inflation, Central Bank Raises Interest Rates  VOI.ID
articles.full_text:
JAKARTA - The surge in energy prices due to the Iran war has prompted a number of major central banks to raise interest rates to curb inflation. However, this move carries other risks. Economic growth could weaken further, even some developed countries could potentially experience a recession by 2027.
According to Anadolu Agency, quoted on Saturday, October 17, the United States Central Bank (The Fed), the European Central Bank (ECB), and the Bank of Japan (BoJ) raised interest rates in September 2026. Meanwhile, the Bank of England (BoE) maintained its interest rate, despite the continued increase in inflationary pressures.
Huw Dixon, professor emeritus of economics at Cardiff University, warned that the energy crisis due to the Iran war had changed inflation forecasts and the direction of monetary policy since the beginning of the year.
He assessed that economic growth could potentially stall by 2027. A recession is also likely in a number of G7 member countries, a group of seven countries with advanced economies.
"Interest rates have to be raised to control inflation. However, we may see interest rates remain high, but below the inflation rate, to limit their impact on the real economy," said Dixon.
The rise in energy prices has left central banks facing a difficult choice. Interest rates need to be raised to hold down inflation, but the cost of borrowing is also hitting households and businesses.
Dixon estimates that central banks will not return to implementing interest rates close to zero as during the 2008 financial crisis, unless there is a conflict with Russia.
US Inflation Soars, The Fed Raises Interest Rates
In the United States, annual inflation rose to 3.7 percent in September, from 3.4 percent in August, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.6 percent. A 9.1 percent jump in gasoline prices accounted for more than half of the increase.
Overall energy prices jumped 20.4 percent compared to a year earlier. Gasoline prices rose 34.2 percent, while heating oil soared 74.2 percent.
Core inflation, which does not include food and energy prices, also rose to 2.6 percent from 2.4 percent. Price increases also occurred in housing costs, education, used vehicles, recreation, and air tickets.
The Fed then raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage point to 3.75-4 percent on September 16. The decision was unanimous.
The US central bank judged that inflation was still high so that a rate hike was needed to help bring it back to the 2 percent target.
However, the Fed still sees the economy as quite strong, supported by domestic spending, productivity growth, and investment.
European Inflation Rises, Britain Begins to Feel the Pressure
In the eurozone, annual inflation is expected to rise to 3.8 percent in September, from 3.2 percent in August, according to Eurostat's initial estimate.
Energy inflation rose to 18.8 percent from 14.3 percent. Inflation in the services sector also increased to 3.2 percent from 3 percent.
The ECB raised its three main interest rates by 0.25 percentage points each on September 10. The deposit facility rate, which is the interest paid to banks for funds deposited at the ECB, rose to 2.5 percent.
The ECB warned that the Middle East conflict could keep inflation above target for a long time.
The central bank estimates that average inflation will reach 3 percent in 2026, then fall to 2.5 percent in 2027 and 2.1 percent in 2028.
However, the ECB still projects the eurozone economy to grow 0.9 percent in 2026 and 1.4 percent in 2027. These estimates differ from Dixon's warning about the possibility of a recession.
The ECB sees higher-than-expected inflation risks, while economic growth is potentially weakening. However, the central bank has not confirmed the direction of the next interest rate.
In the UK, the BoE kept its benchmark rate at 3.75 percent on September 17. Six committee members supported the decision, while the other three wanted a rise to 4 percent.
UK inflation was recorded at 3.1 percent in August. The BoE expects the figure to reach 3.75 percent in the fourth quarter and slightly exceed 4 percent by early 2027.
Dixon said before the US and Israeli attacks on Iran, UK inflation was originally expected to fall to 2 percent in April. Interest rates are also expected to fall to a range of 3-3.5 percent.
Now, he estimates inflation will reach 4 percent by the end of 2026 and potentially rise further in 2027 if the war continues.
"The Bank of England's interest rate will go up," he said.
Although the BoE survey showed that the interest rate forecast lasted for quite some time, the movement of the financial market led to a possible increase. The BoE reminded that market prices are also influenced by risk premiums, which are additional yields that investors ask for to face uncertainty.
The increase in borrowing costs is beginning to be felt by the British public. The interest rate on fixed-rate home loans for two years was recorded at around 0.95 percentage points higher than before the conflict.
Japan Raises Interest Rates Despite Inflation Below 2 Percent
Japan is taking similar steps even though its inflation is lower than that of the United States and Europe.
Japanese annual inflation was recorded at 1.9 percent in August. Meanwhile, inflation excluding fresh food prices reached 1.7 percent.
However, the BoJ still raised its short-term interest rate target to around 1.25 percent on September 18. The decision was supported by seven board members, while the other two opposed it.
The BoJ sees its medium- to long-term inflation forecasts continuing to rise. The central bank is also concerned that wage and raw material cost increases that companies pass on to selling prices will push inflation above its 2 percent target.
The high price of crude oil, the weakening of the yen, and the increasing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) related products also add to the price pressure.
The BoJ expects inflation excluding fresh food to exceed 2 percent in the second half of fiscal 2026. The next rate hike is still open, depending on economic and inflation developments.
Dixon warned prolonged uncertainty could undermine confidence in the central bank's ability to maintain price stability.
"Inflation expectations over the past few years have been relatively contained. However, the current uncertainty is so great that this condition could change if central banks again let inflation get out of control," he said.

articles.title: Gold Slips From $4,190 as Yields and Fed Hike Risk Cap the Range — $4,500 Opens Only Above $4,295 - TradingNEWS
articles.summary: Gold Slips From $4,190 as Yields and Fed Hike Risk Cap the Range — $4,500 Opens Only Above $4,295  TradingNEWS
articles.full_text:
Key Points
- Spot gold fell 0.44% to $4,147.22 after an intraday high of $4,190.70 failed below $4,200.
- Global gold ETF holdings reached a record 4,256 tonnes after $10 billion in September inflows.
- COMEX speculative net longs fell to 210,335 contracts, a two-month low after five weekly cuts.
Spot gold (XAU/USD) traded at $4,147.22 an ounce by late morning in New York on Monday, October 19, 2026, down $18.18, or 0.44%, from Friday’s settlement at $4,165.40. The session started well. Spot opened firm in Asia, traded at $4,175.60 early in the day and printed an intraday high of $4,190.70 before sellers took control. By 10:45 a.m. ET the metal had fallen to $4,145.80 with a session low of $4,142.10, a $48.60 swing from top to bottom.
December COMEX gold futures (GC) followed the same path. They opened at $4,185, briefly cleared $4,200 to touch $4,211.20, then reversed to $4,163.80 by 11:26 a.m. ET, down $17.30 or 0.41% from Friday’s $4,181.10 close. That is the third time in two weeks that futures have pushed through $4,200 and failed to hold it.
The reversal came as risk appetite returned to other markets. The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.67% to 26,575.38, the S&P 500 added 0.85% to 7,724.20, and the VIX fell 11.36% to 17.72. Investors who bought gold for protection during last week’s 4.5% Nasdaq slide had less reason to hold it on Monday. At the same time the 10-year Treasury yield climbed 3 basis points to 5.13% and the dollar index firmed 0.15% to 101.96, two direct headwinds for a metal that pays no income.
The thesis of this forecast is narrow. Gold is trapped between a $4,073 floor built by structural buyers and a $4,200 ceiling enforced by 5%-plus Treasury yields and Fed hike risk. Central banks and gold-backed ETFs keep absorbing supply on every dip: ETF holdings hit a record 4,256 tonnes in September and China’s central bank bought 23 tonnes in the same month. Speculators keep selling every rally, and the 10-year yield refuses to break back below 5%. Neither side has enough force to break the range on its own.
The broader trend argues for patience. Gold trades 26% below its January 28 record of $5,602.22. It is down 4.89% over the past month and 4.45% over 12 months, and it sits $148 below its 200-day exponential moving average at $4,295.10, the line that has capped every rebound since September.
The catalyst that decides the break is fixed on the calendar. The Federal Reserve announces its next decision on October 28, with the funds rate at 3.75% to 4.00% after September’s hike. Until then, the working range is $4,073 to $4,217, and Monday’s failure at $4,200 tilts the near-term bias toward a retest of the floor.
The Intraday Tape: Another Rejection at $4,200
Monday’s session followed a script gold traders have seen repeatedly this month. The Asian open brought buyers. China’s third-quarter GDP growth of 4.5% beat the 4.4% forecast, Brent crude eased from last week’s five-month high near $110, and the 10-year yield dipped to 5.065% in early Asian trading. Spot gold climbed 0.3% to $4,175.60, and December futures rose 0.4% to $4,196.40.
The European session extended the move. By 7:06 a.m. ET, futures traded at $4,190.50, and the COMEX contract briefly broke above $4,200, reaching $4,211.20 on the day. Spot followed to $4,190.70. Indian futures confirmed the bid, with MCX gold trading between ₹147,751 and ₹148,574 per 10 grams.
The reversal began before the New York open. Spot gold slipped to $4,164 by 9:15 a.m. ET and $4,161.54 by 9:00 a.m. ET on another feed, then broke lower once U.S. equities opened and the Nasdaq accelerated. At 9:49 a.m. ET spot traded at $4,162.92, down $9.94. By 10:45 a.m. ET it had fallen to $4,145.80, and the selling held through late morning, with spot at $4,147.22.
The timing tells you who was selling. The drop accelerated precisely as chip stocks rallied 2.3% and the 10-year yield turned higher. Money that had moved into gold during last week’s AI sell-off was rotating back into equities. The 10-year yield’s climb from 5.065% in Asia to 5.13% by late morning added 6.5 basis points of real-yield pressure in a few hours.
The session’s range of $4,142.10 to $4,190.70 fits inside last week’s band of $4,073 to $4,217. Gold has now traded inside that $144 window for two full weeks. The intraday high came within $9.30 of $4,200 on spot and briefly exceeded it on futures, but neither contract closed an hourly bar above the level during New York hours.
The rest of the precious metals complex moved differently. Silver rose 0.79% to $57.76 an ounce, and spot silver traded at $58.03. Platinum gained $8.00 to $1,650.60 and palladium added $10.59 to $1,146.94. The industrial metals benefited from China’s GDP beat and the equity rally, while gold, the pure monetary asset, lost ground. The gold-to-silver ratio fell to 71.8, which shows the rotation from defensive to cyclical exposure inside the metals complex.
The $4,073 to $4,217 Box: Two Weeks of Failed Breakouts
The defining feature of gold’s chart is a tight horizontal range that has held since the first week of October. The floor sits at $4,073, the October low. The ceiling sits at $4,217, the top of last week’s range, with $4,200 acting as the psychological barrier inside it.
The floor has been tested twice. In the week ending October 2, gold posted its sixth consecutive weekly decline and touched its lowest level since August 5, erasing all of August’s gains. On October 5, spot fell 0.9% to $4,153 as yields held near their highest levels since 2002. The low of the month came at $4,073. Then on October 15, the day after the hot September CPI report, spot flushed to $4,099.89 before buyers stepped in and drove it to a $4,138.25 close, up 0.82% on the day.
That October 15 reversal is the strongest piece of evidence for the bull case. Gold rallied on a day when headline inflation printed 3.7%, core inflation printed 2.6%, and October hike odds jumped. Buyers were willing to absorb the worst inflation news of the month at $4,100.
The ceiling has been tested three times. In the week ending October 9, spot closed at $4,194.65, up 1.47% for its first weekly gain in three weeks, and COMEX futures settled at $4,220.30. That close above $4,200 lasted one session. Last week, the range top came at $4,217 before gold slipped 0.7% for the week, with spot settling Friday at $4,165.40 and futures at $4,186.70. On Monday, futures touched $4,211.20 and spot $4,190.70 before the latest rejection.
Inside the box, the structure is clear. Support sits at $4,150 and $4,142, the session low. Below that, $4,100 and $4,073 form the floor. Resistance runs from $4,188 to $4,200, then $4,217 to $4,225. A daily close above $4,225 would be the first confirmed breakout since early September.
The range itself sits well below the levels gold held this summer. In August, spot topped $4,500 for the first time since June, reaching $4,508.28 on August 19 after a 4% single-day gain. In early September it peaked near $4,700, before sliding 8.5% across the month. The current box is a consolidation after that September slide, not a base after a rally.
The 200-Day EMA at $4,295: The Line That Defines the Trend
The single most important technical level on gold’s daily chart is the 200-day exponential moving average at $4,295.10. Spot gold trades $148 below it, a 3.5% gap. Every rebound since the early-September peak near $4,700 has failed below that average.
The 200-day EMA separates a correction inside a bull market from a new downtrend. When gold traded above it through August and early September, dips were bought aggressively. Since price broke below in September, rallies have been sold. The average is also falling, which means the resistance it provides will drift lower over the coming weeks, from $4,295 toward $4,250 if gold stays inside its current range into November.
The longer-term chart shows how far gold has traveled this year. The metal opened 2026 above $4,300 after closing 2025 at a record pace. January delivered a parabolic move: gold added close to $1,100 an ounce in a single month and set an all-time high of $5,602.22 on January 28. The LBMA morning fix peaked at $5,501.70 on January 29. Two days later, gold fell close to $500 in a single session on January 30.
The correction that followed ran into early summer. The LBMA fix bottomed at $3,994.50 in late June, a 27% decline from the January high, with spot basing near $3,950. From there, gold rallied back above $4,500 in August and toward $4,700 in early September before rolling over again.
The current $4,147 price sits 26% below the record, 4% above the June low and 12% below the September peak. Gold is not in freefall, but it is not trending either. It is consolidating in the lower third of its 2026 range.
Momentum indicators are soft without being oversold. Gold’s month-on-month loss of 4.89% from $4,378 and the September decline of 8.5% have pulled momentum readings toward neutral rather than deeply negative territory. Sellers have room to push without running into exhaustion signals.
A daily close above $4,295 would change the picture. It would put gold back above its long-term trend line for the first time since September, flip the average into support, and open the path to $4,500. Until that happens, every rally inside the $4,073 to $4,217 box is a counter-trend move.
Treasury Yields at 5.13%: The Heaviest Weight on the Metal
Gold’s biggest headwind is the bond market. The 10-year Treasury yield traded at 5.13% on Monday, up 3 basis points, after touching 5.065% in Asia. It has held above 5% for most of October and reached its highest levels since 2002 earlier this month.
The mechanism is simple. Gold pays no interest. When a 10-year Treasury pays 5.13% and the 2-year pays 4.72%, the opportunity cost of holding an ounce of gold rises with every basis point. Investors who can lock in 5% on government debt need a stronger reason to hold a zero-yield asset, and that reason has to come from either a falling

articles.full_text:
Oct. 19 (UPI) -- The New York Stock Exchange announced on Monday that it is extending its trading hours for heavily traded stocks.
The NYSE is extending its hours beginning Monday, opening two new trading sessions from 7:30 a.m. to 9:25 a.m. EDT and from 4 p.m. to 4:15 p.m. EDT. Twenty-five single stocks and five exchange-traded funds will be eligible for trade for extended hours.
Major stocks that will have expanded trade availability include Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Oracle and Bank of America.
"Markets have changed tremendously over the years, and that kind of progress only happens when you keep investing in your technology," Kevin Tyrrell, chief product officer for the NYSE, said in a statement. "Extended trading hours for options reflects market demand for investment opportunities and reliable risk management during a longer period of time, and as we look ahead to bringing the same approach to equities in December, we'll continue to treat innovation as the foundation for growth."
The appetite and demand for a 24-hour trading cycle continues to grow, thanks in part to technological innovations such as cryptocurrency exchanges. CBOE research found that extended hours trading is more popular than ever with 199,000 contracts being traded on average each day.
Day one of the NYSE's new extended hours was not remarkably active with less than $100,000 in contracts being moved.
