articles.title: More BoJ’s Ueda names two factors for bond market action, keeps JGB taper plan unchanged - investingLive
articles.summary: More BoJ’s Ueda names two factors for bond market action, keeps JGB taper plan unchanged  investingLive
articles.full_text:
Summary
- Bank of Japan Governor Ueda said the bank’s bond taper stance is unchanged and declined to pre-set when it would act in the JGB market, citing rapid yield rises or destabilising market function as factors. He said appropriate rate hikes help stabilise JGBs.
The yen’s muted response suggests markets saw little new here beyond confirmation of the BoJ’s existing approach. For Japanese government bonds, Ueda’s message cuts two ways: he is not offering a backstop at any particular yield level, yet he is signalling the bank will act if the selloff becomes disorderly. Super-long JGBs, the most sensitive part of the curve, are where any test of that commitment would show up first. His argument that falling behind on rates would push yields higher strengthens the hawkish framing ahead of 30 October. Global bond investors will watch closely, given Japan’s role in global yields and capital flows.
-
Ueda is telling bond markets that the best protection against a disorderly selloff is a BoJ that keeps raising rates on time, not a promise to step in at a set level.
Summary:
- BoJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said there is no change to the bank’s basic stance on tapering its bond purchases
- He said it would be inappropriate to say in advance when the BoJ might conduct emergency bond market operations
- Any decision would weigh market conditions comprehensively, such as a rapid rise in long-term rates or signs of destabilising market function
- He expects long-term rates to rise steadily in line with any increases in the policy rate
- He warned that failing to adjust rates appropriately could push long-term yields higher on inflation overshoot fears
- He said financial conditions remain accommodative; the yen barely moved
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said the central bank’s basic approach to reducing its bond purchases is unchanged, and declined to say in advance when it might step into the government bond market with emergency operations.
Speaking in the same appearance in which he stressed the importance of anchoring underlying inflation around 2%, Ueda said the BoJ would look comprehensively at market conditions before deciding whether to intervene. He pointed to two considerations in particular: whether long-term interest rates are rising at a rapid pace, and whether bond market functioning is showing signs of instability.
Ueda also set out how he expects short and long-term rates to interact as policy tightens. If the BoJ raises its short-term policy rate, he said, long-term rates are likely to rise steadily in line with those steps. But if the policy rate is not adjusted appropriately, he warned, market concerns about the risk of inflation overshooting could push long-term yields higher.
In effect, Ueda argued that well-calibrated rate increases are a stabilising force for the Japanese government bond market rather than a threat to it. By conducting policy appropriately to achieve its 2% inflation goal, he said, the BoJ can help stabilise JGBs. He added that financial conditions remain accommodative, a reminder that policy is still supportive of growth even after the bank’s recent hikes.
The remarks address a tension that has run through the BoJ’s exit from years of ultra-loose policy. The bank has been gradually scaling back its bond buying while raising rates, leaving investors alert to the risk of disorderly moves in long-term yields. By declining to set a trigger for emergency buying, Ueda keeps the bank’s options open while signalling that intervention would be reserved for genuinely disorderly conditions rather than a steady repricing.
The comments also reinforce the hawkish tone of his earlier remarks, framing further rate increases as consistent with market stability. The BoJ’s policy rate stands at 1.25%, with the next decision due on 30 October.
The yen was little changed as Ueda spoke, suggesting the bond market comments largely confirmed existing expectations.

articles.title: Nearly $1M in sports, Pokémon cards stolen from FedEx truck in California - NBC News
articles.summary: Nearly $1M in sports, Pokémon cards stolen from FedEx truck in California  NBC NewsFedEx truck robbed of trading cards worth over $963,000 outside PSA headquarters  The New York TimesOrange County police investigating after $1 million in sports and Pokémon cards stolen from FedEx truck  CBS NewsPSA Responds After More Than $100,000 Worth of Graded Trading Cards Stolen from FedEx Truck  IGNPokémon and sports card collectors outraged as PSA-graded cards stol...
articles.full_text:
Thieves made off with nearly $1 million in sports, Pokémon and other trading cards swiped from a FedEx truck in Southern California last week, police said Monday.
Officers responded to a trading card authentication company Tuesday about the theft of an estimated $963,000 worth of cards from a FedEx truck, Santa Ana police spokesperson Natalie Garcia said by email. The theft included two pallets of cards and a third that was “disrupted,” she said.
The location of the report was Professional Sports Authenticator in the city of Santa Ana, about 33 miles southeast of Los Angeles.
The company bills itself on its website as “the leading third-party authentication and grading service” and says it can sell customers’ cards online for a percentage of the selling price to “turn cards into currency.”
Nick Andrews, known on social media as the Boston Card Hunter, said on X that there are multiple victims of the theft, one of whom he said lost $500,000 worth of cards.
When all is said and done, he said, the heist could be one of the biggest in trading card history.
He has compiled a list of cards claimed to have been taken in the theft that numbered as high as 383 on Monday evening. Among them, as the video game news site IGN noted, were a 1995 Upper Deck 23K Gold Michael Jordan card and a 2024 One Piece Simplified Chinese 1st Anniversary Set Nami.
Card trader Sky-B, who said he wants to be referred to only under that moniker, discussed cards he said he lost in the theft in a video on YouTube on Monday.
“These were 104 cards that I’ve accumulated over two years,” he said. “There are many irreplaceable cards in here that I will never see again. And, honestly, that’s what hurts the most — outside of obviously being absolutely financially destroyed here.”
He said the missing cards were dropped off at Professional Sports Authenticator, where they were certified and started their journey back to him in Michigan before he discovered they had been stolen.
Sky-B said he paid $8,000 in grading fees and lamented that he would be out the likely increased value that the grading added to his cards, which he said were insured up to $156,000 — below their likely market value.
A company spokesperson said in an email that grading fees would be returned, along with the fair market value of the cards involved.
In a statement, the company said it is working with investigators and has deactivated the stolen cards’ certificates.
“We have deactivated the certificates for the stolen items and notified marketplace partners so they can be on the lookout for rare and serialized items,” a Professional Sports Authenticator spokesperson said.
FedEx said in a statement that getting to the bottom of the theft is paramount.
“The security of our customers’ shipments is a top priority, and we are working with local law enforcement in their investigation,” it said.
Garcia, the police spokesperson, said the value of the stolen goods could rise.
“It remains an open case,” she said, “and we have not made any arrests or recovered any stolen goods.”
In 2024, a FedEx shipment of 54 vintage baseball cards worth $2.1 million was successfully delivered to a Best Western in Strongsville, Ohio, for a sports card conference, but it was stolen by a hotel employee who was sentenced to four to six years in prison, prosecutors in nearby Cleveland said.

articles.title: US government bans Chinese AI company DeepSeek that had wiped more than $1 trillion from Wall Street in l - The Times of India
articles.summary: US government bans Chinese AI company DeepSeek that had wiped more than $1 trillion from Wall Street in l  The Times of IndiaUS orders DeepSeek removed from federal systems, citing national security risks  South China Morning PostUS bans DeepSeek AI from government use as tech tension with China continues  BBCUS banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems  Reuters3 US AI Migration Stocks Investors May Revisit After DeepSeek Ban &nbsp...
articles.full_text:
The US Homeland Security Department has ordered the removal of products and third-party services of Chinese AI company Deepseek. In an order, DHS has banned US civilian agency IT systems from using any DeepSeek AI model. The US government is also banning acquisition of products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek technology by US civilian government agencies. In an order, DHS said that DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees or vendors." In its order, DHS also said that the use of DeepSeek by government agencies "could produce actionable intelligence on US persons and/or government agencies. The models themselves may contain malware or other security vulnerabilities."
In a memo passed in July this year, DHS told federal agencies to monitor flows of traffic in and out of government websites to address potential risks from DeepSeek. Previously, several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states including New York, Tennessee, and Virginia have taken similar steps.
When DeepSeek wiped hundreds of billions from WallStreet in one day
Incidentally, DeepSeek is the same Chinese AI company whose low-cost artificial intelligence (AI) model sent shock waves in the US stock market in January 2025. The selloff in the US stock market was prompted by the release of the free AI assistant from China's DeepSeek that the startup said needed less data at a fraction of the cost of services from American technology companies.
DeepSeek worries wiped over a trillion dollars from market value of some of the biggest US companies in semiconductor, power and infrastructure sectors. Nvidia alone lost about 17% or close to $593 billion in market value, a record one-day loss for any company.
What the summary of the DHS order on DeepSeek says
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is publishing notice of the Secretary of Homeland Security’s issuance of an order (1) excluding information technology products and services developed by Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co, Ltd (DeepSeek), to include affiliated entities as defined in applicable regulations, from federal civilian agency procurements; and, (2) removing all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.
FCC to ban Chinese labs from testing US gadgets and equipment
Earlier this month, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said that it will vote on October 29 to bar all Chinese labs from testing electronic devices such as smartphones, cameras and computers for use in the US, widening a previous action targeting Beijing. The FCC said it will prohibit test labs and certification bodies in countries including China that deny reciprocal treatment to US-based test labs. In 2025, the FCC banned testing of US electronics by labs owned or controlled by the Chinese government, and several dozen labs were barred.
FCC Chair Brendan Carr had then said that 82% of electronics were tested in China, which does not have an agreement with the US. But the agency said this year that a substantial majority of China-based test labs were still testing US electronics. "Less than 4% of all electronic devices are tested in labs located inside the US," Carr said, adding the FCC will "insist on fair and reciprocal treatment in international commerce."

articles.title: CSRC to speed up yuan counter trading and REITs in HK Stock Connect - The Standard (HK)
articles.summary: CSRC to speed up yuan counter trading and REITs in HK Stock Connect  The Standard (HK)
articles.full_text:
China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) chairman Wu Qing said China will accelerate yuan counter trading and real estate investment trusts (REITs) within the Stock Connect scheme under a five-synergy cooperation model between the mainland and Hong Kong markets.
Wu Qing said at the Annual Conference of Financial Street Forum 2026 that it is necessary to strengthen strict law enforcement, cultivate a standardized and healthy market ecosystem, fully implement the "five major supervisions," further strengthen the supply of institutional mechanisms, and resolutely safeguard an open, fair, and just market order.
He also laid out four near-term measures, starting with the establishment of a fund operation monitoring center to handle private fund share registration, collect public and private fund information, conduct risk monitoring, and enhance risk prevention, control, and supervisory effectiveness in the fund industry.
The second is to issue opinions on the safe and compliant use of artificial intelligence in securities and futures, strengthen rules on business development and data security, promote secure and efficient application in risk control and investment research, and guide technology for good.
The third is to improve the penalty rules for illegal share reductions, adhere to the principle that penalties match the offence and that neither the innocent nor the guilty are wrongly treated, refine the determination standards, and crack down on illegal share reductions more precisely and effectively.
Lastly, Wu said CSRC will formulate and issue guidance on advance compensation in the securities market, clarify the applicable entities and implementation procedures, promote advance compensation in accordance with the law, quickly and efficiently, and better safeguard the lawful rights and interests of small and medium-sized investors.
He stressed the need to prioritize the safety and stability of the capital market. This includes closely tracking domestic and overseas market developments, strengthening risk assessment and policy tool reserves, and consolidating and improving market stabilization mechanisms.
Wu added that the CSRC will strengthen risk prevention for new businesses and remain highly vigilant against emerging risks, such as overseas leveraged products linked to individual A-share stocks.

articles.title: OpenAI races to secure ₩40 trillion before Anthropic IPO - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
articles.summary: OpenAI races to secure ₩40 trillion before Anthropic IPO - CHOSUNBIZ  Chosunbiz
articles.full_text:
OpenAI is accelerating efforts to raise about $30 billion (about 40.3 trillion won) in funding ahead of rival Anthropic's initial public offering (IPO).
On the 19th (local time), Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, reported that OpenAI is seeking to secure a large pool of investment funds before Anthropic's listing. In this funding round, OpenAI's valuation is expected to exceed $1.4 trillion (about 1,880 trillion won). That would be more than 60% higher than the $852 billion (about 1,144 trillion won) valuation recognized when it raised $122 billion in March.
OpenAI aims to secure investment commitments before Anthropic goes public in mid-November. Because the two companies are raising capital from a similar pool of investors, it is seen as a strategy to lock in funds ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
Existing investors such as SoftBank Group and Abu Dhabi's MGX are reportedly in talks to participate in this funding round. OpenAI is said to have met with long-term investment funds and sovereign wealth funds last week, when Anthropic held an investor presentation.
Demand to invest in both companies is high, but investors must allocate capital to large fundraisings occurring just days to weeks apart. Some investors view OpenAI as moving first to secure money that could be deployed into Anthropic's IPO.
OpenAI has told investors that growth has steepened since the launch of the GPT-6 Astra model. According to one source, OpenAI's annualized revenue currently stands at $50 billion (about 67.1 trillion won) and is expected to rise to $70 billion (about 94 trillion won) by year-end. Another source said OpenAI aims to wrap up fundraising before Anthropic's listing makes its financials public and the two companies' results are directly compared.
The two companies are also sparring over how revenue is calculated. OpenAI has criticized Anthropic for inflating results by recognizing the aggregates of contracts sold through third-party cloud vendors as revenue. Anthropic's stance is that it follows established accounting practices.
Anthropic's revenue rose from $11.6 billion in the second quarter this year to $16.8 billion in the third quarter. However, as monthly revenue growth slows, concerns are emerging about its valuation. Some investors have reportedly suggested setting Anthropic's IPO valuation at around $1.5 trillion, lower than the initially hoped-for $2 trillion.
Investor sentiment toward tech stocks has also been shaky recently. Since September, oil price swings, rising bond yields, and concerns about AI safety have added to market uncertainty. As a result, some corporations have delayed listing plans until after the Anthropic IPO. AirTrunk, backed by Blackstone; PerfMode, backed by Nvidia; and SB Energy, backed by SoftBank, are said to have withdrawn or put their listing plans on hold.

articles.title: Dollar and Euro Continue Their Upward Surge in Cuba's Informal Market - CubaHeadlines
articles.summary: Dollar and Euro Continue Their Upward Surge in Cuba's Informal Market  CubaHeadlines
articles.full_text:
The US dollar and euro are showing no signs of slowing down in Cuba's informal currency market. On Monday, both foreign currencies gained ground against the Cuban peso, closing the day at higher values than they opened with, extending a rising trend that continues to pressure the national currency.
By 8:00 p.m. local time, CiberCuba's exchange rate indicated the US dollar was at 813 Cuban pesos (CUP), while the euro had reached 905 CUP, according to the informal market's benchmark rates.
Both currencies ended the day above their initial quotes, a particularly noteworthy development since the dollar had already hit its highest value in the past 30 days that morning.
Initially, at the start of Monday, the dollar was trading at 812 CUP and the euro at 903 CUP. While the US bill maintained its upward trajectory, the European currency saw a slight decline compared to Sunday.
However, as the day progressed, the scenario shifted.
The dollar gained another peso between its 10:00 a.m. opening and the 8:00 p.m. close, while the euro rebounded, adding two pesos to its starting rate.
In just 12 hours, both currencies rose again against the Cuban peso.
The dollar's progression is particularly notable when compared to Sunday's close of 808 CUP. With the current rate of 813 CUP, the American currency has increased by five pesos in a single day.
On a weekly basis, the dollar has seen a rise of 25 pesos, climbing from 788 CUP a week ago, marking an approximate 3.2% variation.
This trend is even more pronounced over the past month.
Thirty days ago, the dollar's informal reference was around 709 CUP. With its current rate, the difference stands at 104 Cuban pesos.
Regardless, the dollar concluded Monday at a higher level than recorded in the morning, continuing its upward path over the last week.
The euro also showed no mercy to the Cuban peso. Starting Monday at 903 CUP, it ended the day at 905 CUP, regaining its early losses.
This figure marks an increase of two pesos over Sunday's closing value, which was also at 903 CUP. Daily statistical references indicate an approximate variation of 2.5 pesos due to underlying index values.
Over the past week, the euro has surged by 20 pesos, up from 885 CUP seven days ago, equating to an approximate 2.3% increase.
Monthly comparisons also highlight a significant gain: from 805 CUP 30 days ago to the current 905 CUP, a 100 peso difference.
The euro maintains its status as the most expensive of the main informal market references in Cuba, with a 92 peso difference compared to the US dollar.
While both cash currencies advanced, the Freely Convertible Currency (MLC) exhibited a different trend.
Its indicative value closed Monday at 593 CUP, below the 637 CUP it marked earlier in the day.

Why are the dollar and euro rising in Cuba's informal market?
The increase in the dollar and euro in Cuba's informal market can be attributed to various economic pressures and limited foreign currency supply, causing these currencies to appreciate against the Cuban peso.

articles.title: Treasury Weighs Cuts to Long-Term Bond Auctions Ahead of November 4 - SuaraGarut.ID
articles.summary: Treasury Weighs Cuts to Long-Term Bond Auctions Ahead of November 4  SuaraGarut.ID
articles.full_text:
The US Treasury is signaling a possible shift in its long-term borrowing strategy as elevated bond yields and weak investor demand complicate government debt financing. A dealer questionnaire has raised expectations that the department could reduce auction sizes for 20-year and 30-year Treasury bonds at its November 4 refunding, according to an October 18 analysis by The Dark Side of the Boom.
The potential adjustment follows an earlier intervention by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in response to rising US yields. Bloomberg reported on October 15 that Bessent's approach initially affected the market but also departed from the Treasury's longstanding practice of maintaining predictable debt issuance to minimize borrowing costs over time.
Jason Williams and Citi's US rates strategy team interpret the latest Treasury questionnaire as a possible signal of changes to the supply of long-term government debt. Although the questions focus on liquidity, market functioning and investor demand, their analysis suggests the department may be preparing to reduce the volume of bonds offered at upcoming auctions.
The long end of the Treasury market has faced a combination of weak demand, elevated yields and substantial competing debt issuance. Reducing the supply of longer-dated securities could address some of these pressures, although the Treasury has continued to frame the relevant issues around market functioning rather than explicitly announcing an issuance change.
Citi expects a reduction in long-term bond issuance to shift more of the government's financing burden toward Treasury bills. Such a change would alter the composition of federal borrowing rather than eliminate the government's overall funding needs.
The possible shift also comes as changing conditions in technology stocks have affected the role of government bonds in investment portfolios. The Dark Side of the Boom analysis said a reversal in artificial intelligence-related market positions had made Treasuries more useful as a hedge, potentially strengthening their appeal to investors.
Bloomberg's October 15 report highlighted the implications of Bessent's earlier response to rising yields. The intervention came as the Trump administration faced pressure to deliver lower borrowing costs, a stated policy objective that had become harder to achieve as Treasury yields climbed.
The episode also raised questions about the Treasury's established approach to debt management. For decades, the department has emphasized regular and predictable issuance as a way to secure the lowest borrowing costs over time. Bloomberg's account said Bessent's actions effectively broke with that longstanding framework.
The next major test of the potential supply adjustment is the Treasury's November 4 refunding, when changes to the 20-year and 30-year auction sizes could clarify whether the department intends to respond to market conditions by reducing long-term issuance.

Indeed, at the start of the day this Monday, the dollar was quoted at 812 CUP and the euro at 903 CUP. While the U.S. dollar continued its upward trend, the European currency experienced a slight decline compared to Sunday.
However, the situation changed as the hours went by.
Exchange Rate Evolution
The dollar gained another peso between the opening at 10:00 a.m. and the closing at 8:00 p.m., while the euro regained some ground, adding two pesos to its initial rate.
In just twelve hours, both currencies rose again against the Cuban peso.
The evolution of the dollar is particularly significant when compared to its close on Sunday, when it was valued at 808 CUP.
With the current 813 CUP, the US dollar has experienced an increase of five pesos in a single day.
On a weekly basis, the dollar has gained 25 pesos, having stood at 788 CUP seven days ago, a change equivalent to approximately 3.2%.
The trend is even more pronounced when observing the behavior of the last month.
Thirty days ago, the informal reference for the dollar was around 709 CUP. With its current rate, the difference amounts to 104 Cuban pesos.
In any case, the dollar ends Monday at a level higher than that recorded in the morning and continues on an upward trajectory over the past week.
The euro also showed no mercy to the Cuban peso. The European currency, which started on Monday at 903 CUP, closed the day at 905 CUP, regaining the ground it lost at the beginning of the day.
The figure represents an increase of two pesos compared to the rounded value at the close on Sunday, which was also at 903 CUP. The statistical references used for daily comparison indicate an approximate variation of 2.5 pesos, due to the underlying values of the index.
In the last week, the euro has risen by 20 pesos, from 885 CUP recorded seven days ago, which amounts to an approximate increase of 2.3%.
The monthly comparison also shows a significant increase: from the 805 CUP recorded 30 days ago to the current 905 CUP, a difference of 100 pesos.
The euro also maintains its position as the most expensive of the main benchmarks in the Cuban informal market, with a difference of 92 pesos compared to the US dollar.
While both cash currencies advanced, the Freely Convertible Currency (MLC) exhibited a different trend.
Its indicative value at the close on Monday was 593 CUP, down from the 637 CUP it indicated in the morning.

articles.title: Ambani looks to pull off India’s biggest IPO - Financial Times
articles.summary: Ambani looks to pull off India’s biggest IPO  Financial TimesJio Platforms' anchor book draws record ₹2.5 lakh crore in bids ahead of IPO  The HinduHow Jio grew from a 2016 launch to India’s largest IPO in a decade  The Times of IndiaJio Platforms raises Rs 8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors ahead of Rs 30,188-crore IPO; LIC, Capital...  Moneycontrol.comJio Platforms draws about $25 bn in IPO anchor investor bids  VCCircle
articles.full_text:
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter.
India’s second-richest man will try to pull off the country’s biggest listing in the teeth of a stock market downturn, tougher competition and goading from Elon Musk.
Jio Platforms, a telecoms behemoth backed by Meta and Google, opened orders on Monday for what is set to be India’s biggest-ever initial public offering and one of its few tied to cutting-edge technology.
A listing “of this kind, of this scale” only happens “once in a generation”, said Yatin Singh, chief executive of investment banking at Emkay Global Financial Services in Mumbai.
But the $3bn offering, which has been seven years in the making since billionaire Mukesh Ambani first floated the idea, comes at a challenging time for the company credited with bringing millions of Indians online with its cheap broadband service.
Global wars and their impact on oil have put its parent company, Reliance Industries, under immense stress. A lack of AI champions has left Indian equities out of favour with foreign capital, and the Ambanis have struggled to convince foreign investors of their intended lofty valuation.
Jio is aiming for a $107bn valuation, a considerable drop from its initial expectations of more than $150bn when it filed a draft prospectus this summer.
The family-owned conglomerate has prodded its more than 400,000 employees to buy into the issue ahead of Jio’s expected debut next week.
“The Ambanis have always encouraged a culture of building equity, and it should start from home,” said a person aware of the plans, adding that Reliance was “facilitating” participation for employees who wanted to bid for shares.
Vivekanand Subbaraman, an analyst at Ambit Capital in Mumbai, said the valuation cut was “not a Jio-specific issue” but “more an India recalibration”.
“The mobile segment is saturated and there isn’t much scope to grow subscribers at a very fast pace any more,” he said.
Cornerstone investors made bids of $26bn on Monday, more than 30 times the allotted quota, according to a person familiar with the matter. An exchange filing showed funds including BlackRock and Fidelity, as well as Singapore’s government, were allotted shares.
Jio was founded in 2016 with the goal of bringing faster internet access to India’s nearly 1.5bn people.
Isha Ambani, a director on Jio’s board and daughter of Mukesh, told investors last week that the business idea came after she and her brother Akash returned from studying in the US and could not file an assignment because of poor connectivity.
“What followed was a conversation about why should India be left behind,” she said.
The group initiated a brutal price war and quickly undercut its competition by offering plans for as little as $2 a month. By June this year, Jio had 533mn users — about a third of the country’s population — ranking it third among the world’s telecom companies by subscribers. Its closest domestic rival, Bharti Airtel, has 492mn users in India.
In 2020, Meta acquired a 10 per cent stake. Google followed with a near 8 per cent stake. Despite its success in attracting customers, analysts have questioned Jio’s ability to make more revenue from its wide user base.
“If you look at telecoms in India, we’re reasonably well penetrated now,” said Singh. “Any growth from here on will be a function of [average revenue per user] growth.”
Analysts at Nomura said Airtel remained their top pick for the sector “due to its higher proportion of premium subscribers”, which should insulate it from user attrition following expected tariff increases later this year.
Akash Ambani, the chair of Jio and eldest son of Mukesh Ambani, said last week that the IPO funds would be used to reduce the company’s net debt and argued that Jio had “very large” headroom for growth beyond higher tariffs.
“Giving the most affordable services with the best form of quality has been Jio’s hallmark from day one, and that is what we’ll keep pursuing,” he said.
Jio also has ambitions to provide satellite internet services. Last year, it signed a partnership with SpaceX to sell Starlink equipment in India.
However, it is also a competitor to Musk’s company as it has its own low-orbit satellite business. New Delhi has not granted any applicant a final licence for satellite broadband services.
This month, Musk accused Mukesh Ambani of using his influence to block Starlink’s entry into India, calling him “Prime Minister Ambani” and “the real boss of India”.
Jio responded in a statement: “We welcome competition in satellite communications, including Starlink.”
Apart from plans for wireless and mobile services, Akash Ambani told Reliance shareholders in June that the group was investing in AI, building data centres through its Reliance Intelligence arm and developing voice-based AI models in 22 Indian languages.
Despite the tech ambitions, oil refining remains the Ambanis’ cash cow. The business has come under severe strain as the war in Iran disrupts oil flow from the Middle East and US President Donald Trump pressures India to not buy Russian crude.
As a result, Reliance Industries has underperformed India’s already flagging market, falling 23 per cent this year compared with a 12 per cent decline in the blue-chip Nifty 50 index. Analysts said the poor market conditions added to pressure on Jio’s IPO.
“The way Indian markets have been operating at least since June is you go out with an ask and investors will then put a haircut to it,” said Singh.
Nomura analysts pointed out that Jio’s current target valuation would give it an enterprise value to ebitda ratio of 10.9, higher than rival Airtel’s 9.2, which might not sit well with some investors.
Jio’s IPO is part of succession plans for Reliance Industries as Ambani splits his $170bn empire into three standalone businesses, with Akash leading Jio, Isha heading retail and Anant, the youngest, helming energy.
Kranthi Bathini, director of equity strategy at WealthMills Securities in Mumbai, said Jio’s data and new-technology businesses would play “a key role” in Reliance’s growth and for the Ambani children who will eventually take the reins.
“For them, the success of the IPO is extremely crucial,” he said.

articles.title: How far can foreign currencies rise in Cuba? Another day of increases for the dollar and the euro in the informal market - CiberCuba
articles.summary: How far can foreign currencies rise in Cuba? Another day of increases for the dollar and the euro in the informal market  CiberCuba
articles.full_text:
opens this Sunday, October 18, 2026, with a new upward trend.
At 10:00 a.m. (Cuban local time), the U.S. dollar rises to an average of 807 Cuban pesos, the euro climbs to 904 pesos, and the Freely Convertible Currency (MLC) stands around 652 pesos.
Exchange rate summary
- Exchange rate of the USD to CUP: 807 CUP
- Exchange rate of the euro EUR to CUP: 904 CUP
- Exchange rate from MLC to CUP: 652 CUP (indicative value, limited data)
The dollar is on the rise
The US dollar is trading at 807 Cuban pesos (CUP) in the informal market this Sunday.
This represents an increase of two pesos compared to the previous day, when it closed at 805 CUP.
The bullish trend is also evident on the weekly horizon: seven days ago, the greenback was trading at 783 pesos, reflecting an increase of 24 pesos over the last seven days, which amounts to a rise of 3.1%.
Exchange Rate Evolution
Compared to 30 days ago, when the exchange rate was at 703 pesos, the accumulated increase has risen to 104 pesos (+14.8%), although this month-to-month comparison may partially reflect adjustments in the methodology of the index and not solely market movement.
The dollar also reached its highest point in the last 30 days precisely in today's session, at 807 CUP.
The euro, the most expensive currency in the parallel market
The euro is quoted at 904 Cuban pesos (CUP), three pesos above the 901 recorded on the previous day.
In the last week, the European currency has gained 26 pesos compared to the 878 CUP from seven days ago, an increase of 3.0%.
In the monthly outlook, the euro has risen by 101 pesos from 803 CUP thirty days ago (+12.6%). However, as is the case with the dollar, this variation should be interpreted with caution since it may include methodological adjustments to the index.
The highest recorded in the last 30 days is 905 CUP, just one peso above the current level.
It is stated as the most expensive currency in the Cuban parallel market, exceeding the dollar by 97 pesos and consolidating its dominant position.
The MLC, a indicative figure with strong weekly variation
The MLC appears this Sunday at around 652 Cuban pesos (CUP), 18 pesos above the 634 from the previous day.
However, this value should be taken with caution: the source indicates it comes with a warning of limited data during this time period, so it serves as a guiding figure.
In weekly terms, the change is striking: seven days ago, the MLC was at 497 pesos, which implies an increase of 155 pesos in seven days (+31.2%).
Compared to 30 days ago, when it was priced at 454 pesos, the accumulated increase is 198 pesos (+43.6%), although this monthly comparison may also reflect methodological adjustments to the index.
Without a physical existence, its use is limited to state-run businesses that accept it, which restricts its circulation compared to cash currencies.
The gap with the official rate is becoming increasingly wide
The official exchange rate of the Central Bank of Cuba (Segment III), at 720 CUP per dollar and 811 CUP per euro, remains well below the values that prevail in everyday practice in the informal currency market.
The difference between the official and informal prices currently stands at 87 pesos for the dollar and 93 pesos for the euro.
In the last 30 days, the official exchange rate of the dollar has risen from 667 to 720 CUP, and that of the euro, from 765 to 811 CUP, a pace of adjustment that has not succeeded in narrowing the gap with the parallel market.

- 1 USD = 807 CUP.
- 5 USD = 4,035 CUP.
- 10 USD = 8,070 CUP.
- 20 USD = 16,140 CUP.
- 50 USD = 40,350 CUP.
- 100 USD = 80,700 CUP.
Equivalence of euro bills (EUR) to Cuban pesos (CUP) based on the exchange rates this Sunday, October 18, 2026:
- 1 EUR = 904 CUP.
- 5 EUR = 4.520 CUP.
- 10 EUR = 9,040 CUP.
- 20 EUR = 18,080 CUP.
- 50 EUR = 45,200 CUP.
- 100 EUR = 90,400 CUP.
Methodology
The CiberCuba Exchange Rate is an index of the Cuban informal market created from the automated analysis of thousands of currency trading posts in Telegram and Facebook groups.
The calculation eliminates atypical offers and spam messages, weighs each transaction based on its age, and consolidates a representative value that is updated several times a day.

articles.title: EUR/USD consolidates at the lows as France's budget and US CPI remain in focus - investingLive
articles.summary: EUR/USD consolidates at the lows as France's budget and US CPI remain in focus  investingLive
articles.full_text:
Summary
- The US dollar remains supported by risk-off flows amid French fiscal concerns, despite a dovish repricing of Fed expectations. Markets will focus on Wednesday’s US CPI report, with hotter core inflation potentially reviving rate hike bets and boosting the greenback. Meanwhile, the euro’s outlook hinges on developments in France, where the proposed deficit reduction to 5.0% of GDP could help stabilise bond markets, although parliamentary risks remain. US-Iran negotiations and energy prices will also influence inflation expectations and central bank policy.
The US dollar has been supported recently despite a dovish repricing triggered by Fed’s Williams and Fed’s Jefferson comments that pushed back against expectations of a rate hike in October.
The main reason were risk-off flows into the greenback due to European debt concerns. The focus has been particularly on France, where political uncertainty and concerns over the country's large fiscal deficit have recently pushed French government bond yields higher and widened the spread over German Bunds to its highest level since the eurozone debt crisis.
A stabilization in French spreads could allow some of the euro's risk premium to unwind and trigger a pullback in the US dollar, while further widening and contagion to other countries would likely keep the greenback supported.
Moreover, the US-Iran negotiations continue to be at a stalemate but at least Trump ruled out new strikes before the November elections last week. This week, we also have the US CPI report on the agenda, which could trigger big moves in the markets.
A hotter than expected core CPI could bring a rate hike in October back on the table and give the US dollar a boost. A soft report, on the other hand, will likely weigh on the greenback in the short-term on a fall in Treasury yields.
On the EUR side, the probabilities of an ECB rate hike in October have faded following the sharp widening in the French-German bond spread, as policymakers are likely to remain cautious about adding further pressure to already fragile financial markets.
However, markets still expect the ECB to raise rates in December, reflecting persistent inflationary pressures due to higher energy prices. In terms of economic data, the latest Eurozone CPI showed headline inflation surging to 3.8% in September from 3.2% in August, largely due to higher energy prices. Core inflation remained relatively contained, edging up to 2.5% from 2.4%.
Looking ahead, energy prices and developments in the Middle East will remain important drivers of the inflation outlook. Any sustained decline in energy prices could reduce near-term inflation pressure and give the ECB more room to delay further tightening. This would also be positive for the euro on improved risk sentiment and lower Fed rate hike expectations.
The euro will also remain sensitive to developments in the bond market, particularly the French-German spread. France’s government has proposed a 2027 budget targeting a deficit of 5.0% of GDP, supported by spending restraint and higher tax revenues. This is lower than the previously 5.4% and helped ease market concerns somewhat. However, the plan still faces parliamentary hurdles, and Eurozone finance ministers and the ECB have urged France to pass a credible budget to restore market confidence.
Traders will keep a close eye on France where improvements would be positive for the euro, while negative outcomes will likely continue to weigh on the single currency.
EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME
On the daily chart, we can see that EURUSD has been selling off heavily in the past weeks on France’s debt woes. The nearest key support is around the 1.1067 level. If the price gets there, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a recovery into the major downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to increase the bearish bets into the 1.08 handle next.
EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME
On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the selloff since early September. The sellers will likely continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break to start positioning into the major downward trendline, with the 1.1285 level as the first target.
EURUSD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 1 HOUR TIMEFRAME
On the 1 hour chart, we can see that the pair has been bottoming out since the French proposed budget deficit for 2027 got lowered to 5.0% from 5.4%. We have a support zone around the 1.1160 level. The buyers will likely continue to step in around the support, with a defined risk below it, to keep targeting a break above the trendline and new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to increase the bearish bets into new lows. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
UPCOMING CATALYSTS
On Wednesday we have the US CPI report. On Thursday, we get the US PPI, the US Retail Sales and the latest US Jobless Claims figures.

articles.title: Statement by Christine Lagarde, President of the ECB, at the fifty-fourth meeting of the International Monetary and Financial Committee - Disruption Banking
articles.summary: Statement by Christine Lagarde, President of the ECB, at the fifty-fourth meeting of the International Monetary and Financial Committee  Disruption Banking
articles.full_text:
IMF Annual Meetings, 17 October 2026
Introduction
The global economy has proven surprisingly resilient in the face of high uncertainty. The conflict in the Middle East continues to expose energy markets to sharp swings. Trade tensions and protectionist measures are weighing on confidence and contributing to a reconfiguration of trade flows. The global economy has held up thanks in part to the rise of artificial intelligence, with investment in technology supporting activity and trade, particularly in economies integrated into technology value chains. Risks nonetheless remain tilted to the downside for growth and to the upside for inflation. A return to an international economic order grounded in openness, predictability and the rule of law would help trade and investment flourish.
Economic activity
Despite global headwinds and the ongoing energy shock, the euro area economy has so far proved resilient. Growth was broad-based across most euro area countries and sectors in the first half of 2026. The September ECB staff projections foresee growth of 0.9% in 2026, 1.4% in 2027 and 1.5% in 2028.
As the energy shock fades over the medium term, the projections see domestic demand benefitting from a recovery in real income over the medium term, driven by lower energy inflation and a resilient labour market. Rising government spending on infrastructure and defence, complemented by investment in AI and digital technologies, should also support growth. Export growth should pick up on the back of strengthening foreign demand, also driven by AI.
The medium-term outlook is surrounded by uncertainty over how intense and long-lasting the Middle East conflict will be, and how the resulting shocks might propagate through the economy. Risks to growth are assessed to be on the downside.
Fiscal sustainability remains a crucial anchor for broader economic stability. It is important to maintain sound fiscal policies, including by adhering to fiscal rules, and, where debt is high, to consolidate, re-prioritise spending and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of public finances to rebuild buffers. Governments should strive to ensure that any fiscal response to the energy shock is temporary, targeted and tailored.
In addition, policies that strengthen resilience to climate change can improve the economy’s ability to absorb climate-related shocks. These efforts should be complemented by structural policies that promote labour market participation, equip the workforce with the skills needed in an AI-driven economy and facilitate the diffusion of new technologies. Priorities include advancing the savings and investments union, improving access to risk capital and creating better conditions for innovative firms to scale up across the Single Market.
Inflation
Headline inflation increased to 3.8% in September, mostly reflecting a surge in energy inflation, and, to a lesser extent, an increase in food and services inflation. Core inflation increased slightly to 2.5%. The range of underlying inflation measures remained broadly stable in September and wages have so far shown no material response to the energy shock.
Looking ahead, higher energy prices are expected to keep headline inflation well above target into the first half of 2027 and to gradually feed through to core and food inflation. Headline inflation is expected to decline after the first quarter as energy inflation falls, returning to around target towards the end of 2027. The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside due, in particular, to the Middle East conflict and Russia’s unjustified war against Ukraine. A more intense or persistent energy shock could strengthen indirect and second-round effects, resulting in higher and more persistent inflation. Extreme weather could push up food prices. By contrast, a sustainable resolution of geopolitical conflicts, weaker energy pass-through or more risk-averse financial markets could lower inflation.
Monetary policy
The Governing Council decided to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points in September, following an increase of the same size in June.
Our interest rate decisions are based on our reaction function, which comprises three criteria: our assessment of the inflation outlook and the risks surrounding it, in light of the incoming economic and financial data, the dynamics of underlying inflation; and the strength of monetary policy transmission.
The inflation outlook points to higher inflation ahead, especially in the short term, given the latest developments in energy markets. However, we see no evidence at this stage of significant pass-through of energy prices to other prices and wages, beyond what we have already included in our projections. And while growth has been resilient, financing conditions have tightened, with long-term interest rates rising notably since our last meeting. This will slow growth and reduce pass-through by more than projected in our September exercise.
Taking these three criteria together, the energy shock is too large to “look through” but a measured response remains appropriate to keep inflation in check.
In setting future policy, we will make a comprehensive assessment of the incoming data based on our reaction function. In July, the Governing Council decided on the operational features and the onboarding process for the enhanced EUREP, the Eurosystem repo facility for central banks that was announced earlier this year. The new facility supports the smooth transmission of monetary policy and reinforces the international role of the euro. More than 30 central banks have expressed interest in EUREP in the past six months.
Financial stability
Sources of risk and vulnerabilities for euro area financial stability remain high. Continued geopolitical tensions, fiscal challenges and uncertainties around accelerated AI adoption continue to be causes for concern. The widespread concentration of critical third-party service providers introduces single points of failure for both financial and non-financial institutions. New frontier AI models have increased cyber risks and operational vulnerabilities.
Euro area banks maintain strong capital and liquidity buffers and robust profitability, together with healthy and stable asset quality. These solid fundamentals should help navigate ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and effectively support lending to the economy. Strengthened prudential regulation and supervision since the global financial crisis has helped leave euro area banks in a strong position to withstand the unfolding economic challenges.
Shocks could expose vulnerabilities among non-bank financial intermediaries, notably from concentrated AI-related exposures, amplifying market stress and creating spillovers across financial sectors. Banks’ exposures to non-banks and vulnerable firms could expose funding and credit vulnerabilities.
Stress in private credit markets has continued, with private credit funds reporting outflows and reactivating redemption gates. Private market “semi-liquid funds” that allow for redemptions are becoming more prevalent, which could lead to greater liquidity mismatches in the future, but euro area financial institutions have limited direct exposure to private credit. This means, for now, that private credit in isolation is unlikely to be a source of financial instability in the euro area.
Payment systems
Central bank money must evolve to fulfil the needs of an increasingly digital economy. The Eurosystem is at the forefront of this evolution, bringing the stability and trust of central bank money to digital retail payments and tokenised finance in Europe. In the retail space we are preparing to complement cash with its digital equivalent – the digital euro – for day-to-day payments. The digital euro will further stimulate innovation and competition in retail payments, ensuring that the continued co-existence of public and private solutions underpins Europe’s strategic autonomy in payments. To lay the groundwork for a seamless and secure launch, we will run a 12-month internal pilot in the second half of 2027. Adopting the Regulation on the establishment of the digital euro by the end of 2026 is key to making this possible.
In the wholesale space, the Eurosystem is developing new capabilities to ensure that central bank money can settle transactions in the growing market of tokenised assets. Pontes – the Eurosystem’s distributed ledger technology (DLT) solution that went live on 21 September – marks the first step in implementing our strategy to enable the development of a European tokenised ecosystem. This vision will be advanced under the Appia initiative, which aims to deliver a blueprint for this ecosystem based on common standards, shared network infrastructure and European governance.
International cooperation
We value the work of our global institutions and fora, particularly those that promote global macroeconomic and financial stability. We welcome the recent completion of the three major IMF reviews (Comprehensive Surveillance Review, Financial Sector Assessment Program Review and Review of Program Design and Conditionality), which strengthen the role of the IMF at the centre of the global financial safety net. Climate-related work should remain fully anchored in IMF operations, particularly surveillance. Multilateral efforts to help tackle global imbalances support coordination of domestic action that is required to minimise the risks from disorderly adjustment. The IMF’s analytical work on global imbalances and its improvements to the methodology for assessing external balances provide a strong basis for these efforts.

articles.title: The Bank of Canada may significantly raise its inflation forecast, leaving open the possibility of raising interest rates. - Vietnam.vn
articles.summary: The Bank of Canada may significantly raise its inflation forecast, leaving open the possibility of raising interest rates.  Vietnam.vn
articles.full_text:
|  | 
| Image: Wikimedia Commons (CC0 1.0). | 
 Oil prices increase the risk of prolonged inflation.
 On October 17, Governor Tiff Macklem said the Bank of Canada (BoC) expects to significantly raise its inflation forecast in its quarterly economic outlook report to be released this month, due to persistently high prices for crude oil and petroleum products.
 New forecasts on inflation and economic growth will be key inputs for the Bank of Canada's interest rate decision-making process at its meeting on October 28.
 “With the conflict in the Middle East continuing, oil shipments remaining restricted, and refining capacity impacted by damaged infrastructure, the risk of widespread and prolonged inflation has increased,” Macklem told reporters in a phone call from Bangkok, on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings.
 According to the head of the Bank of China (BoC), the current challenge lies not only in the rising prices of oil and energy products, but also in the potential for these pressures to spill over into other sectors of the economy. This is a crucial factor that the central bank needs to consider when determining its monetary policy direction in the coming period.
 "Our 2% inflation target is our guiding principle, and we are committed to maintaining inflation close to this target in the long term. We are prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed," he said.
 These statements indicate that the Bank of China (BoC) is paying particular attention to the risk that the energy price shock is no longer temporary, but could create prolonged upward pressure on prices, further complicating the task of controlling inflation.
 The market expects the Bank of Canada (BoC) to raise interest rates by 100 basis points in 2027.
 Despite rising inflation concerns, financial markets are not yet expecting the Bank of Canada (BoC) to adjust interest rates at any of its remaining meetings this year. According to Reuters, as of October 17th, the money market had not yet reflected the possibility of a BoC rate hike at its October 28th meeting or its final policy meeting of the year in December. However, expectations of a rate increase have risen in recent months, with the market anticipating a total increase of 100 basis points, or 1 percentage point, by 2027.
 Referring to the policy decision to be made on October 28, Mr. Macklem said: “The question we will have to consider is whether inflation can fall back to target on its own or whether we will have to raise interest rates to influence and adjust the inflation trajectory in a way that brings inflation closer to target?”
 Besides energy price pressures, the Bank of China (BoC) governor also mentioned broader challenges to the global economy. According to him, the world economy has demonstrated resilience to conflicts in the Middle East and the Russia- Ukraine conflict, but this resilience is being tested by rising costs and tighter financial conditions.
 Mr. Macklem also noted that governments have limited fiscal space, requiring policy adjustments to restore their ability to respond to future economic shocks.

Jio Platforms’ upcoming IPO has reportedly attracted nearly ₹2.5 lakh crore in commitments, reflecting strong interest from major global and domestic institutional investors ahead of the public issue.
Global investors, including sovereign wealth funds and prominent asset managers such as Allianz and BlackRock, have reportedly expressed interest in participating in the anchor book of the ₹30,188-crore offering. The IPO is expected to be the largest in India’s history.
Domestic institutions, including the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, are also among the prospective investors, according to media reports.
Other investors reportedly interested in the anchor allocation include the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation (GIC), Fidelity, Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, New World Fund Inc and Smallcap World Fund Inc.
Jio Platforms IPO GMP today, or grey market premium, is +235. Considering the upper end of the IPO price band and the current premium in the grey market, the estimated listing price of Jio Platforms share price was indicated at ₹1,354 apiece, which is 21% higher than the IPO price of ₹1,119.
In the past 15 sessions, the IPO GMP has fluctuated by ₹87, shifting between levels without establishing a clear trend. The most recent GMP is ₹235, indicating a shift in grey market expectations, as noted by analysts.
Jio Platforms IPO price band has been fixed at ₹1,065– ₹1,119 per share, with investors required to bid for a minimum of 12 shares and in multiples of 12 thereafter. Eligible employees applying under the reserved category will be entitled to a ₹54 per share discount.
The public issue will open for subscription on 21 October and close on 23 October, while the anchor investor bidding window is scheduled for 19 October. The offering will comprise a fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale (OFS) component.
The company has earmarked up to ₹2,500 crore in shares for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and up to ₹500 crore for eligible employees, bringing the combined reservation to ₹3,000 crore.
Individuals and Hindu Undivided Families holding publicly listed Reliance Industries shares as of 14 October can apply under the shareholder quota, subject to the eligibility criteria outlined in the prospectus and applicable regulations. The employee quota is available to eligible Jio Platforms employees.
Jio Platforms intends to use part of the IPO proceeds to prepay up to ₹27,500 crore of borrowings at its operating subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. The balance will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.

articles.title: Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell's 6-Word Warning Echoes Louder Than Ever -- and It Should Rightly Terrify Wall Street - The Motley Fool
articles.summary: Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell's 6-Word Warning Echoes Louder Than Ever -- and It Should Rightly Terrify Wall Street  The Motley Fool
articles.full_text:
This has been a year packed with history-making moments on Wall Street. We've watched the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -0.07%), S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.41%), and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +1.11%) climb to several record highs, and witnessed the largest initial public offering in the stock market's storied history.
Perhaps the most defining moment of 2026 is the changing of the guard at our nation's central bank. On May 22, Kevin Warsh officially succeeded Jerome Powell as Fed chair. President Donald Trump's nominee to replace Powell has wasted little time reforming the Federal Reserve.
Jerome Powell waded into a subject rarely touched on by Fed chairs. Image source: Official Federal Reserve Photo.
But even though Powell is no longer head of the central bank -- he remains on the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve -- his words still hold plenty of weight on Wall Street. More than a year after delivering a speech in Rhode Island, a six-word statement from the now-former Fed chair echoes louder than ever through Wall Street.
Jerome Powell boldly went where few Fed chairs have gone before
During Powell's two terms as Fed chair, he delivered dozens of speeches and fielded countless questions from reporters. It was rarely a challenge for the press to get Powell to discuss the labor market or touch on the catalysts affecting inflation.
However, one subject that sitting Fed chairs rarely discuss is stock valuations. The head of the central bank doesn't want to be responsible for influencing equity markets. This is something we've repeatedly witnessed from current Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who's shied away from offering forward-looking guidance in any form.
Kevin Warsh just ended his first ever FOMC meeting as Fed chair. His message to markets: "I can't give you any guidance on what we're going to do next." Here is what he said: 1. Inflation is still way above the Fed's 2% target and prices are too high for most people 2. "We will fix five years of misses on inflation", he is directly saying the previous Fed failed 3. The Fed will no longer tell you in advance what it plans to do with interest rates 4. He watches stock market prices more than anything else when making decisions 5. Interest rates are hurting the housing market but are not slowing down financial markets 6. All 19 members at the table agreed not to raise rates today 7. The 2% inflation target is not changing 8. He refused to say whether bond yields rising after today's decision concerns him 9. He refused to say whether he has spoken to Trump since becoming Fed chair Under Powell, the Fed always told markets what was coming next. Under Warsh, that is gone.
— Bull Theory (@BullTheoryio) June 17, 2026
But once in a blue moon, a sitting Fed chair will weigh in on equity valuations, if and only if those valuations somehow pose a threat to the integrity of credit markets and/or the health of the U.S. economy, including the job market.
In December 1996, then-head of the central bank, Alan Greenspan, delivered what became known as the "irrational exuberance" speech at the American Enterprise Institute. Greenspan's speech covered the rapid rise in stock valuations amid the advent and proliferation of the internet.
In September 2025, Powell had a mini-Greenspan moment. While responding to a reporter's question about how the Fed accounts for equity valuations in monetary policy, Powell offered a rare observation about stock valuations:
We do look at overall financial conditions, and we ask ourselves whether our policies are affecting financial conditions in a way that is what we're trying to achieve. But you're right, by many measures, for example, equity prices are fairly highly valued.
This six-word response, "equity prices are fairly highly valued," is a warning shot fired across the bow of Wall Street.
While game-changing technologies, such as the internet, have previously supported premium stock valuations for a few years, history says that extended valuations aren't sustainable over the long run.
Image source: Getty Images.
The second-priciest stock market over the last 156 years (likely) isn't sustainable
Given that there isn't a one-size-fits-all blueprint to value individual stocks or the broader market, valuation is one of the trickiest subjects to discuss. Even Alan Greenspan's irrational exuberance speech was, in hindsight, delivered more than three years before the dot-com bubble burst in March 2000.
There is, however, one time-tested valuation tool that's done a remarkable job of providing investors with apples-to-apples valuation comparisons of the S&P 500. More importantly, this valuation tool has a knack for foreshadowing short-term directional moves in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite. I'm talking about the S&P 500's Shiller Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio).
What helps the Shiller P/E Ratio stand out is that it factors in trailing earnings over the previous decade. Whereas the traditional P/E, which uses trailing 12-month earnings, can be tripped up by recessions if earnings turn negative, this isn't a concern for the Shiller P/E Ratio.
Introduced by economists in 1988, the CAPE Ratio has been back-tested to January 1871. Over the last 156 years, it's averaged a multiple of 17.42. As of the closing bell on Oct. 12, this valuation tool was approaching a multiple of 42, just a stone's throw away from its all-time high of 44.19, set just three months before the dot-com bubble burst.
Stock Market Shiller PE Ratio on the verge of taking out its Dot Com Bubble all-time high 🚨 🤯 👀 https://t.co/CtCmSgWnLt
— Barchart (@Barchart) July 11, 2026
Over the last century, the Shiller P/E has surpassed 30 during a continuous bull market on six occasions, including the present. The previous five occurrences all eventually saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and/or Nasdaq Composite plunge between 20% and 89%. For instance, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq shed 49% and 78% of their respective values on a peak-to-trough basis after the dot-com bubble burst.
While the S&P 500's CAPE Ratio has an uncanny ability to foreshadow what's next for stocks, it offers no help in pinpointing precisely when the music will stop or which catalysts will push stocks over the proverbial cliff. Nevertheless, Jerome Powell's six-word warning about equity prices is historically spot-on.
The one thing to always keep in mind is that while historical precedent can offer dire short-term forecasts, history is an undeniable ally of patient, optimistic investors. Looking back more than a century, there hasn't been a rolling 20-year period in which Wall Street's benchmark index has delivered a negative average annual total return, including dividends.
If former Fed Chair Jerome Powell's stock valuation warning proves prescient, consider it an opportunity to pounce on great companies at bargain prices.

articles.title: Bitcoin price outlook for November: Can BTC recover after the Fed decision? - Crypto News
articles.summary: Bitcoin price outlook for November: Can BTC recover after the Fed decision?  Crypto News
articles.full_text:
Bitcoin enters the final weeks of October near $82,000 after a brief fall below $80,000. The October 28 Federal Reserve decision, uneven demand for U.S. spot funds and November inflation data will help determine whether the recovery survives. A forecast requires conditions for both gains and losses, not a single number detached from the evidence.
- Bitcoin traded near $81,500 on October 17 after briefly dipping below $80,000 this week.
- September U.S. inflation reached 3.7% annually, up from 3.4% in August.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin funds lost a net $614.7 million across October’s first 12 trading sessions, based on Farside’s daily totals.
- The Fed meets October 27 and 28, before U.S. jobs data on November 6 and inflation data on November 10.
- A move from $82,000 to $90,000 requires a 9.8% gain; a drop to $75,000 would be an 8.5% loss.
Bitcoin has traded around $81,500 on October 17, having recovered from a move below $80,000 during the week. CoinGlass market data put the 24 hour change near negative 0.7% when checked for this article. A live price can move before publication, so the scenarios below use $82,000 as a rounded reference point, not a claim about the exact execution price available to a reader.
The Federal Reserve’s calendar places its next policy decision on October 28. Inflation has complicated the choice: the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ September CPI release put annual headline inflation at 3.7%. November will bring new employment and consumer price readings, giving investors evidence on whether the October decision was the start of another tightening phase or a single step. The price outlook therefore has two clocks: what markets expect before the meeting, and what the incoming data say afterward.
Bitcoin’s October recovery has a weak demand backdrop
The starting point is less reassuring than the bounce suggests. Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 and subsequently recovered above $82,000 on October 16. A separate October 16 price assessment at crypto.news placed the market near $81,400 and noted the sequence of lower local highs. Clearing a level intraday is different from sustaining buying through several sessions, especially when the same area has served as both support and resistance.
October’s price movement followed several conflicting signals. U.S. spot Bitcoin funds began the month with two positive sessions, then recorded substantial withdrawals on October 7 and 8. The October 7 fund outflow reached $484.9 million, the largest daily exit since June at the time. October 13 brought $175.7 million back, but October 14 saw $261.4 million leave. Farside Investors’ daily fund table now records an $82.4 million withdrawal for October 16. Daily totals can be revised, and a net flow is not a direct measure of exchange spot purchases on that date.
Price and flow do not have to move together. Bitcoin trades continuously, while the U.S. ETF table reflects the close of an equity trading day. A buyer using an offshore exchange or a derivatives position can move the price while the fund complex loses assets. Authorized participants can acquire or deliver Bitcoin through creation and redemption processes that need not match a single hour of trading. Treating each positive close as proof that ETFs bought the rebound would assign a cause that the available figures cannot establish.
The October 14 CPI report added a macroeconomic complication. Headline consumer prices rose 0.6% during September, while the measure excluding food and energy rose 0.3%. Gasoline accounted for more than half of the monthly increase in the headline index, according to the BLS. Annual core inflation reached 2.6%, below the 3.7% headline reading but above August’s 2.4%. A reader looking only at the headline could miss that the sources of inflation are different; a reader looking only at core could miss the pressure that energy prices put on household spending and market rates.
Bitcoin’s drop after the CPI release left the market near $81,900 on October 14. The report recorded an increase in market-implied odds of an October rate increase after the inflation data, but those odds are a changing price of futures contracts, not a vote by the Fed. They should be checked again near the decision. Positioning against a policy announcement can make an otherwise ordinary price move violent when leveraged traders have crowded into one outcome.
The Fed decision is only the first date on November’s calendar
On September 16, the Federal Open Market Committee raised its target by a quarter percentage point to 3.75% to 4%. The vote was unanimous. Its next scheduled meeting ends October 28 at 2 p.m. Eastern time, followed by a press conference at 2:30 p.m. The October meeting is not marked as one of the scheduled quarterly projection meetings on the Fed’s calendar, so investors should not assume it will include a new dot plot.
The September meeting minutes, released October 7, say most participants considered another increase likely to be appropriate by year end, while stressing that later decisions depended on incoming information. Year end leaves two meetings, October and December. The minutes do not commit the committee to October, and individual September projections are conditional judgments, not instructions to a future meeting. The September median projected policy rate at the end of 2026 was 4.1%, according to the Fed’s projection tables.
Bitcoin rallied after the September rate increase despite fund withdrawals during the decision window. An examination of buyers after the September hike found subsequent ETF demand and derivatives adjustment, showing why the rate announcement alone cannot explain the entire move. Traders had been preparing for the decision beforehand; the same announcement can lift or lower an asset depending on what was already priced in and what the chair says about future policy.
On October 28, the rate decision, statement, and press conference, should be read separately. A quarter point increase with language suggesting a pause would not carry the same implication as an increase followed by concern about more persistent inflation. A hold could still weigh on Bitcoin if officials signal another hike in December. Market prices respond to changes in expected policy paths, not simply to the label attached to one decision.
November’s scheduled releases will then test the Fed’s reading of the economy. The BLS calendar for November lists the October employment report for November 6, October CPI for November 10, and October producer prices for November 13. October CPI will arrive after the Fed meeting, meaning the committee cannot use that report to decide on October 28. It can still change expectations for the December 8 and 9 meeting. Figures and release dates should be rechecked at publication because government calendars can change.
The sequence allows a conditional outlook. An October decision followed by softer inflation and moderate employment growth could ease pressure on bond yields. A decision followed by stubborn inflation or a much stronger labor market could support expectations of more tightening. A weak jobs report is not automatically favorable for Bitcoin if it points to a broad economic shock that sends investors toward cash. None of the official releases predicts a Bitcoin price; they influence the rates and risk appetite against which Bitcoin trades.
Twelve ETF sessions show how much buying the recovery needs
The distinguishing figure comes from adding the fund flows rather than citing a single large withdrawal. Farside’s U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF table lists daily totals, in millions of dollars, for the first 12 trading sessions of October: plus 102.7, plus 189.9, minus 89.8, plus 118.8, minus 484.9, minus 244.1, plus 21.1, minus 65.4, plus 175.7, minus 261.4, plus 5.1 and minus 82.4. Adding those published entries gives minus $614.7 million through October 16. The calculation uses the displayed one decimal place and may differ slightly if a provider later revises individual funds.
Across the same 12 sessions, positive days total $613.3 million and negative days total $1.228 billion after rounding the entries. Net outflows are therefore the result of several heavy selling days overwhelming the purchases, not the absence of any positive session. October 7 alone accounts for approximately 79% of the net withdrawal figure, a ratio obtained by dividing $484.9 million by $614.7 million. That ratio describes the arithmetic concentration of the monthly total, not an estimate that one day’s redemptions caused 79% of Bitcoin’s price change.
Four of the first 12 sessions show net gains above $100 million, while four show losses above $80 million. A small positive day does not erase a large negative day. For example, the $175.7 million gained on October 13 was smaller than the $261.4 million lost the next day; together they represent an $85.7 million withdrawal. October 15’s $5.1 million intake did little to counter the $82.4 million that left on October 16. These comparisons explain why a chart of alternating green and red bars can look balanced even when the month is firmly negative.
The calculation answers a narrower question than some headlines imply. It does not tell us how much Bitcoin was sold on exchanges, which participants bought any supply offered, or whether a fund’s holdings changed by the same dollar amount as its flow. Net flow is an accounting estimate for money entering or leaving the listed products. Assets under management fluctuate with Bitcoin’s price. Trading volume can surge even when net flow is zero, because shares can change hands between investors without new fund shares being created.
The starting imbalance creates an observable condition for November. A durable recovery supported by fund demand would require multiple positive sessions large enough to offset withdrawals, not merely a return to zero on one day.
